videos.t: 1. Introduction to Human Behavioral Biology
videos.s: The opening lecture of Robert Sapolsky's Stanford course on human behavioral biology, a long lecture series on how biology shapes behavior.
videos.w: Commenters call it an excellent, free introduction to neurobiology, neuroendocrinology and ethology that they think every physician should watch.

videos.t: Sugar: THE BITTER TRUTH
videos.s: Robert Lustigs UCTV lecture Sugar: The Bitter Truth, a pediatric endocrinologist explaining the biochemistry of fructose and its role in metabolic disease.
videos.w: Commenters call it a compelling, entertaining breakdown of why sugar is harmful and say it changed how they approach primary care.

videos.t: Brené Brown on Empathy
videos.s: A short animated talk by Brené Brown on the difference between empathy and sympathy.
videos.w: Clinicians and students cite it for the point that empathy means connecting with the feeling, useful for patient conversations and listening.

videos.t: Easier IV Placement
videos.s: A short demonstration of an IV insertion technique that uses a flash, lift and advance sequence to avoid blowing the vein.
videos.w: Commenters say it raised their IV success rate and helped them stop blowing so many veins.

videos.t: Dimensional Analysis for Nurses & Nursing Students for Dosage Calculations Nursing School
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN explains dimensional analysis for medication dosage calculations for nursing students.
videos.w: Commenters call it the clearest explanation of dimensional analysis they have seen and say it made med math tests easy.

videos.t: The Fall hospital scene
videos.s: A trauma-team resuscitation scene from the TV drama The Fall.
videos.w: Commenters call it the most realistic depiction of a trauma resuscitation on screen and a good look at how a skilled operator runs it.

videos.t: ECG Basics | How to Read & Interpret ECGs: Updated Lecture
videos.s: A long Ninja Nerd lecture on ECG fundamentals and how to read and interpret a 12-lead, taught with hand-drawn diagrams.
videos.w: Viewers say it is long but worth it, with simple explanations of ECG physiology that get you started on 12-leads.

videos.t: How do you avoid a clean kill with wide complex tachycardias?
videos.s: A Hippo EM talk with Dr. Mattu on how to avoid a clean kill with wide complex tachycardias, including why amiodarone can be dangerous in hyperkalemia.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains with cases why giving amiodarone is dangerous in hyperkalemia and how to separate wide complex rhythms.

videos.t: Fluorescein and Push-Pull Contamination
videos.s: A demonstration by LifeFlow using fluorescein dye to show how push-pull action contaminates syringes and saline flush contents.
videos.w: Nurses call it the best demonstration of the syringe contamination principle, and one says it changed their practice.

videos.t: Flying⚡️Doctor ~R.I.P.~ Dr.✜John☘️Hinds✔️ ✅ . The_Fastest Road Racing Doctor,
videos.s: A lecture by the late Dr. John Hinds on the management of motorcycle trauma, including pre-hospital care and trauma arrest.
videos.w: Commenters say his lecture style is captivating and the talk is a good discussion of reversing the things that matter in trauma arrest.

videos.t: Learn How To Suture - Best Suture Techniques and Training
videos.s: A suturing tutorial by plastic surgeon Dr. Zenn covering suture techniques and training.
videos.w: Students say it covers all the suturing they need for rotations and the knots, and works best paired with practice.

videos.t: Introduction to Anatomy & Physiology: Crash Course Anatomy & Physiology #1
videos.s: The opening episode of CrashCourse Anatomy & Physiology, a broad introduction to how the body is organized and studied.
videos.w: Commenters say it is basic but gives the foundation for anatomy and physiology.

videos.t: How to insert difficult IV or draw blood sample in patients with difficult veins: Best technique
videos.s: A NYSORA video on techniques for placing a difficult IV or drawing blood in patients with difficult veins, including the Esmarch bandage method.
videos.w: Commenters call the Esmarch technique incredible and say the video has good information on starting an IV, including the BP cuff method.

videos.t: Ring removal technique: Using an oxygen mask strap
videos.s: A short ALiEM demonstration of removing a ring from a swollen finger using an oxygen mask elastic strap instead of cutting the ring.
videos.w: Several clinicians say they used the technique on a real patient and that it was gentle and worked.

videos.t: Diagnosis Wenckebach
videos.s: A parody clip that works as a Wenckebach heart block explainer.
videos.w: Commenters call it a helpful explanation of Wenckebach and a favorite medical parody.

videos.t: Your Body Language May Shape Who You Are | Amy Cuddy | TED
videos.s: Amy Cuddys TED talk on how body language and power poses may shape confidence.
videos.w: Students recommend it for interview anxiety, with power poses to practice before an interview.

videos.t: Stanford's Sapolsky On Depression in U.S. (Full Lecture)
videos.s: A Stanford lecture by Robert Sapolsky on depression, linking it to neurotransmitters and the biology of the illness.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a fantastic lecture on the biology of depression.

videos.t: Electrocardiography (ECG/EKG) - basics
videos.s: An Osmosis introduction to the basics of the electrocardiogram, covering what an ECG records and how to start reading one.
videos.w: Nurses and students recommend it as an EKG warm-up before arrhythmia and telemetry material.

videos.t: How to Master ABG's (Arterial Blood Gasses)
videos.s: NurseMendoza explains how to interpret arterial blood gases with the tic-tac-toe approach.
videos.w: Commenters say it made ABGs finally click with a simple, memorable approach.

videos.t: Short Electrolytes Memorization Video
videos.s: A short SimpleNursing video on memorizing fluid and electrolyte basics.
videos.w: Students say it keeps fluids and electrolytes simple and got them through the unit.

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1109 - Matthew Walker
videos.s: A Joe Rogan Experience podcast episode with sleep scientist Matthew Walker about sleep and its importance.
videos.w: Commenters suggest it as a good listen, for example on a commute.

videos.t: Brian Goldman: Doctors make mistakes. Can we talk about that?
videos.s: A TED talk by Brian Goldman, an emergency physician, on how medical culture treats mistakes and whether doctors can talk about them.
videos.w: Clinicians say it helps them accept and forgive their own errors and see mistakes as chances to improve the system.

videos.t: Biostatistics SUMMARY STEP 1 - USMLE The Extra stuff
videos.s: The second Randy Neil, MD biostatistics video for USMLE, covering the additional topics beyond the basics with worked problems.
videos.w: Commenters recommend watching both Randy Neil videos and say the worked problems clarify the calculations.

videos.t: Nursing School | How To Read A Textbook
videos.s: Nurse Nacole explains how to read a nursing textbook without reading every word.
videos.w: Commenters repeatedly recommend it for reading nursing textbooks effectively and efficiently.

videos.t: Why You Should Put YOUR MASK On First (My Brain Without Oxygen) - Smarter Every Day 157
videos.s: A Smarter Every Day episode in which the host experiences hypoxia in a chamber to show how oxygen lack affects thinking.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows how cognition declines as hypoxia and hypercapnia develop.

videos.t: Nursing School | How To Study From A Textbook Effectively
videos.s: Nurse Nacole explains how to study from a nursing textbook effectively.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows how to read a textbook and keep up when short on time.

videos.t: Essential Ideas for Parents
videos.s: Russell Barkley's roughly three-hour lecture on ADHD aimed at parents. It explains what ADHD is and how the ADHD brain differs.
videos.w: One commenter calls it the best explanation of ADHD they have seen, and others say it changed how they understood the condition.

videos.t: An easy way to remember arm muscles PART 1
videos.s: Part 1 of a video series on remembering the muscles of the arm, with a playlist covering the forearm and brachial plexus.
videos.w: Students say the videos make sense of the upper limb muscles and locked in upper limb anatomy.

videos.t: Emergency Medical Services: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A Last Week Tonight segment by John Oliver on the state of emergency medical services in the US, including funding, pay and how EMS is classified.
videos.w: EMS workers say it voices complaints they have raised for years and is worth watching.

videos.t: The medical test paradox, and redesigning Bayes' rule
videos.s: A 3Blue1Brown explainer on the medical test paradox, showing how Bayes' rule links test results to the probability of disease.
videos.w: Clinicians and students say it clarifies the limits of test characteristics and helps explain results to patients.

videos.t: The truth about prescription discount cards
videos.s: A pharmacist explains how prescription discount cards work and why he considers them a scam.
videos.w: Pharmacy commenters call it a good, simple overview of how the discount cards operate.

videos.t: RJ Walker - Deceit & I
videos.s: Slam poem by former EMT RJ Walker about a bad call, performed for Button Poetry.
videos.w: EMS workers say it captures how they felt after a similar call and helps them process trauma.

videos.t: Dimensional Analysis for Nursing
videos.s: A video teaching dimensional analysis for nursing dose calculations, including weight-based doses.
videos.w: Commenters say it helped a lot and that the presenter explained med math well.

videos.t: Medical TV Shows Be Like....
videos.s: A comedy sketch from nurse creator Nurse Blake poking fun at how medical TV shows portray hospital work.
videos.w: Nurses share it for the laughs and the jokes about medical show mistakes.

videos.t: Marty Lobdell - Study Less Study Smart
videos.s: A Pierce College lecture by Marty Lobdell on how to study effectively, covering time use, breaks and learning habits.
videos.w: Commenters call it an excellent hour-long lecture on learning better, which helped some who kept failing exams.

videos.t: Adam Ruins Everything - The Real Reason Hospitals Are So Expensive | truTV
videos.s: An Adam Ruins Everything comedy segment on why US hospitals are so expensive, covering opaque price lists, surprise bills and penalties for the uninsured.
videos.w: Commenters offer it as a comic explanation of US medical costs, insurance providers and uninsured penalties.

videos.t: DNA and RNA Viruses Mnemonic for USMLE Step 1
videos.s: A roughly 13-minute flow-chart mnemonic from Matt Skovgard that organizes DNA and RNA viruses for USMLE Step 1.
videos.w: Students call it a favorite for thinking through virus classification and say it helped them memorize viruses.

videos.t: Penn and Teller on Vaccinations
videos.s: A Penn and Teller segment on vaccines, including the claimed link to autism.
videos.w: Commenters send it to skeptics, saying it gets to the point of why vaccination matters.

videos.t: USMLE Biostatistics STEP 1 (1 of 4) Dallas, TX
videos.s: Part 1 of a four-part Randy Neil, MD biostatistics series for USMLE Step 1, with example problems.
videos.w: Commenters say the four videos cover the basics, including cohort versus case-control, and fixed their biostats errors.

videos.t: Just A Routine Operation
videos.s: A Laerdal Medical film in which a husband describes his wife's death after a routine operation, tracing it to failures of communication and human factors.
videos.w: Commenters say every clinician should watch it for the lessons on learning from errors, often compared with aviation.

videos.t: Tim Minchin's Storm the Animated Movie
videos.s: An animated version of Tim Minchin's beat poem Storm, a comic argument against alternative medicine and woolly thinking.
videos.w: Medical students and nurses recommend it as a funny, pointed piece on how misinformation draws people to alternative medicine.

videos.t: Paramedics Force 5 Bridge Creek and Moore, OK Tornado May 3 1999
videos.s: Documentary-style footage of paramedics triaging and treating patients after the 1999 Moore, Oklahoma tornado.
videos.w: Commenters say it illustrates what a nightmare mass casualty incidents are, and one instructor used it in teaching.

videos.t: Head-to-Toe Assessment Nursing | Nursing Physical Health Assessment Exam Skills
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN walks through a head-to-toe nursing assessment, including cranial nerve checks.
videos.w: Commenters recommend saving it as a full walkthrough of the head-to-toe process with helpful tips.

videos.t: How To Use Anki Like A Pro [Full Step-By-Step Walkthrough]
videos.s: TheMDJourney gives a full step-by-step walkthrough of using Anki, including making cards quickly from lecture screenshots and image occlusion.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains Anki so it makes sense and suggest it for anyone giving the app another try.

videos.t: Dr. Michael Greger | How Not To Die | Talks at Google
videos.s: Dr. Michael Greger's Talks at Google lecture on How Not to Die, covering leading causes of death and lifestyle prevention.
videos.w: Commenters say it covers the top killers in developed countries and the lifestyle strategies against them, and some think all doctors should see it.

videos.t: Dialysis: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on dialysis in the United States, focused on the dialysis industry and the largest provider, DaVita.
videos.w: Commenters call it clear, easy-to-follow information on dialysis plus an expose of the industry and its repercussions.

videos.t: Is Most Published Research Wrong?
videos.s: A Veritasium video on why many published research findings can turn out to be false, even when studies are run properly.
videos.w: Commenters across medical communities point to it as a clear visual explanation of how false positives arise in research.

videos.t: How the NRMP Matching Algorithm Works
videos.s: The official NRMP video explaining in about five minutes how the residency Matching Algorithm works.
videos.w: Commenters say it clears up Match misconceptions and shows why applicants should rank by their own preference.

videos.t: Mastering EKGs - A Course Introduction
videos.s: Introduction to Dr. Eric Strong's Mastering EKGs video course, a playlist that builds ECG interpretation from the basics.
videos.w: Commenters across student, nursing and physician subreddits name this playlist as the best way to learn or relearn ECGs.

videos.t: Low Back Pain
videos.s: A DocMikeEvans whiteboard video that summarizes the evidence on treatments for low back pain.
videos.w: Commenters call it a simplified evidence review and an excellent resource to share with patients.

videos.t: Master Your Sleep & Be More Alert When Awake
videos.s: A Huberman Lab podcast episode on improving sleep and alertness during the day.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains sleep and focus in lay terms with references, and found the advice helpful.

videos.t: How Coronavirus Kills: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) & COVID 19 Treatment
videos.s: A MedCram lecture on how COVID-19 causes acute respiratory distress syndrome and how it is treated.
videos.w: Commenters say it refreshed their understanding of the lungs and ARDS, including for those who do not work in the ICU.

videos.t: 12 Lead Interpretation Part 1: Introduction to the 12 Lead EKG
videos.s: The first video of a 12-lead ECG interpretation series, introducing the 12-lead EKG and building toward systematic reading.
videos.w: Commenters say they always recommend this series because it explains the why behind 12-leads with visuals and memory tricks.

videos.t: Anki:How to Miss a Day (making up skipped days or studying ahead without a penalty)
videos.s: The AnKing video on how to miss a day in Anki, making up skipped days or studying ahead without penalty.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for catching up, skipping days and scattering reviews with the Rememorize add-on.

videos.t: Heart embryology video
videos.s: A heart embryology video that walks through how the heart develops.
videos.w: Students say it clarified heart embryology details they struggled with, though it leaves out a few details and works best as an overview.

videos.t: Medical Acid Base Balance, Disorders & ABGs Explained Clearly
videos.s: The first video of a MedCram series on acid-base balance and how to interpret arterial blood gases.
videos.w: Learners say the series makes acid-base and ABG interpretation understandable, with an approach followed by worked problems.

videos.t: What Bodies Think About: Bioelectric Computation Outside the Nervous System - NeurIPS 2018
videos.s: Michael Levin's NeurIPS 2018 talk on bioelectric computation outside the nervous system. It shows how electrical networks among cells shape development and regeneration.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an introduction to Levin's work on how body tissues process information, even for people without a biology background.

videos.t: Dosage Calculations Nursing Practice Problems & Comprehensive NCLEX Review
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN covers dosage calculation practice problems and NCLEX review for nursing students.
videos.w: Commenters call the dosage calculation videos a lifeline for students who are not comfortable with math.

videos.t: How to Download Anki and Begin Using It (we now recommend 2.1!)
videos.s: The AnKing beginner video on downloading Anki and starting to use it, with an associated playlist for new users.
videos.w: Commenters send newcomers here as the starting point for learning Anki basics such as tags.

videos.t: Viscerosomatics for COMLEX
videos.s: A video on viscerosomatic reflexes and Chapman points for the COMLEX osteopathic manipulative medicine exam, drawn out on paper.
videos.w: Osteopathic students say drawing the charts makes this heavily tested material quick to memorize.

videos.t: Introducing MRI: The Basics (1 of 56)
videos.s: The first of 56 lectures on MRI physics by Dr. Michael Lipton of Albert Einstein College of Medicine, starting with the basics.
videos.w: Radiology trainees call the series a great, thorough course and a starting point for understanding MRI physics.

videos.t: We Were Taught to Call Death a Blessing
videos.s: CGP Grey narrates an animated adaptation of Nick Bostrom's Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant. The dragon that demands a toll of lives stands in for aging and society's acceptance of death.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a concise, entertaining way into the argument that aging could be treated as a problem to solve.

videos.t: The Farmer Pain Scale
videos.s: Dr. Glaucomflecken's comedy sketch about the Farmer Pain Scale, a humorous take on how patients rate their pain.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a good, funny demonstration of the scale from a creator who does not mock patients.

videos.t: The BEST Anki Settings and Algorithm Explained (by an expert!)
videos.s: The AnKing explains how the Anki algorithm works and which settings to use.
videos.w: Students cite it for recommended settings that avoid ease hell and for add-on advice.

videos.t: The great porn experiment | Gary Wilson | TEDxGlasgow
videos.s: Gary Wilson's TEDxGlasgow talk arguing that internet pornography overstimulates the brain's reward system and that symptoms can reverse when people stop. TED notes that several claims are not backed by respected academic studies.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as support for the idea that porn can be addictive and that resetting dopamine circuits helps motivation.

videos.t: Hinds: Crack the Chest. Get Crucified.
videos.s: SMACC conference talk by John Hinds on resuscitative thoracotomy, its purpose and survival statistics.
videos.w: Commenters call it an engaging, funny talk that sums up what thoracotomy is actually about.

videos.t: Doc Vader Vs. Patient Satisfaction Scores
videos.s: A ZDoggMD satirical sketch in which Doc Vader takes on patient satisfaction scores, staffing ratios and the hospital as a battle station.
videos.w: Nurses and doctors say it explains why satisfaction scores are flawed and rings true, with laughs.

videos.t: Dr. Cox explaining fun
videos.s: A Scrubs scene in which Dr. Cox speaks about coping with the job, dark humor and distancing from patients.
videos.w: Residents say it captures dark humor in healthcare and the distress of harming a patient, and rewatch it often.

videos.t: The Evolution of Bacteria on a “Mega-Plate” Petri Dish (Kishony Lab)
videos.s: A time-lapse from Harvard's Kishony Lab showing bacteria evolving resistance across a giant antibiotic petri dish.
videos.w: Commenters call it a splendid, simple demonstration of antibiotic resistance emerging, useful for explaining it to patients.

videos.t: Hesi A2 Math| EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ! |Full Review|
videos.s: Nurse Shai gives a full review of the math section of the HESI A2 nursing entrance exam.
videos.w: Commenters say it covers everything on the HESI math portion.

videos.t: CVS Worker has heart attack "NOT ALLOWED" to leave until replacement shows | #PizzaIsNotWorking
videos.s: A commentary from Joshua Fluke on a report of a CVS worker said to be denied leave after a heart attack, framed around poor pharmacy working conditions.
videos.w: Pharmacy commenters share it to show CVS working conditions and to warn about the harm pharmacy school can do.

videos.t: How to Defeat Jet Lag, Shift Work & Sleeplessness
videos.s: Huberman Lab episode on jet lag, shift work and sleeplessness, framing shift work as chronic jet lag.
videos.w: Shift workers in anesthesia and EMS point to it for its explanation of sleep timing, though one notes the host is a bit of a salesman.

videos.t: Short ABGs & Acid Base Imbalances Video
videos.s: A short SimpleNursing video on ABGs and acid-base imbalances, covering compensation.
videos.w: Students say it gave a simple way to approach ABG questions and finally made them make sense.

videos.t: Systolic murmurs, diastolic murmurs, and extra heart sounds - Part 1 | NCLEX-RN | Khan Academy
videos.s: Part 1 of a Khan Academy Medicine series on systolic and diastolic murmurs and extra heart sounds, aimed at NCLEX and clinical learners.
videos.w: Students say it goes through all the murmurs, explains how each arises and cleared up the topic right away.

videos.t: Inside a Covid I.C.U., Through a Nurse's Eyes | NYT Opinion
videos.s: A New York Times Opinion video showing a COVID intensive care unit from the perspective of a nurse.
videos.w: Commenters call it the most honest footage of nursing during COVID and say it shows the physical and emotional toll.

videos.t: Why Did I Fail That Nursing Test?
videos.s: Megan McClintock explains common study and test-taking mistakes that cause nursing students to fail exams.
videos.w: A nursing instructor says she shows her students this video in the first week and that it improved test scores.

videos.t: How to Remember the Cranial Nerves
videos.s: A video teaching the twelve cranial nerves with a finger-based memory method, including how to test them at the bedside.
videos.w: Commenters say the finger method made the nerves stick and helped with testing them during head-to-toe assessments.

videos.t: EMT Review One
videos.s: EMT Review One, a video series reviewing content for the NREMT exam.
videos.w: Commenters say it helped them prepare for the NREMT and was more useful than the EMT course itself.

videos.t: Being Mortal (full documentary) | FRONTLINE
videos.s: The full PBS Frontline documentary Being Mortal, in which Atul Gawande examines how medicine handles aging, serious illness and end-of-life choices.
videos.w: Nurses say they watched it in nursing school and have returned to it across their careers.

videos.t: Pharmacology Made Easy (Part 1) - Common Medication Endings | Picmonic Nursing
videos.s: Part 1 of a free Picmonic pharmacology series for nursing students, covering common drug name endings with visual mnemonics.
videos.w: Students say the series helped them and one credits it for a very high HESI score.

videos.t: It's Not Burnout, It's Moral Injury | Dr. Zubin Damania on Physician "Burnout"
videos.s: Dr. Zubin Damania (ZDoggMD) argues that what clinicians call burnout is better described as moral injury. The talk is aimed at physicians and other healthcare workers.
videos.w: Healthcare workers say it puts words to what they feel and that the burnout-versus-moral-injury framing hits close to home.

videos.t: My stroke of insight | Jill Bolte Taylor | TED
videos.s: Neuroscientist Jill Bolte Taylor gives a first-person account of watching her own brain functions shut down during a massive stroke, losing speech, motion and self-awareness.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a firsthand account from a brain researcher of life when the right hemisphere is in control.

videos.t: Penn & Teller's: Bullshit! - Vaccinations Intro
videos.s: The intro of a Penn and Teller Bullshit! episode on vaccination, a short rant against the anti-vaccination argument.
videos.w: Commenters call it an easy-to-take takedown of anti-vaccine claims that explains why vaccines are needed.

videos.t: ADHD: Essential Ideas for Parents - Dr. Russell Barkely
videos.s: Russell Barkley's nearly three-hour lecture of essential ideas about ADHD for parents. It covers executive function, motivation, emotion and how ADHD affects children.
videos.w: Commenters say it reframes ADHD beyond attention deficit, and one notes the first ten minutes are enough to be enlightening.

videos.t: Psychiatric Interviews for Teaching: Mania
videos.s: A University of Nottingham teaching video with an actor portraying a patient with mania during a psychiatric interview.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best depiction of mania they have seen and praise the acting.

videos.t: Medical School Anki Beginner Tutorial | AnKing Deck
videos.s: A beginner tutorial on Anki for medical school, covering setup, downloading the AnKing deck and add-ons.
videos.w: Students say it covers the basic settings and is all most people need to get started.

videos.t: Structure and Function of the Lung
videos.s: A lecture on the structure and function of the lung from Dr. John West's pulmonary physiology series, hosted by the Qualcomm Institute.
videos.w: Students call Dr. West the best respiratory physiology lecturer and say the series taught them more than textbooks.

videos.t: Controlling Your Dopamine For Motivation, Focus & Satisfaction
videos.s: Andrew Huberman's long podcast episode on dopamine. It covers the neural circuits, peaks and baselines, depletion, and a set of tools for motivation, focus and avoiding addiction.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for a science-based account of motivation and for tips on work paralysis and smartphone use.

videos.t: How my friend ranked 1st at Medical School - The Active Recall Framework
videos.s: Ali Abdaal describes the active recall framework used by a friend who ranked first at medical school, including Anki cards.
videos.w: Commenters say they cannot recommend the method enough and that it improved exam scores.

videos.t: H's & T's: reversible causes of cardiac arrest
videos.s: A retro RPG-styled video illustrating the H's and T's, the reversible causes of cardiac arrest.
videos.w: Commenters say it made each H and T condition understandable, even for laypeople.

videos.t: Infant Developmental Milestones [UndergroundMed]
videos.s: An UndergroundMed video reviewing infant developmental milestones for exam preparation.
videos.w: Commenters say it covers the higher-yield milestones memorably and kept them from missing exam questions.

videos.t: This is how you treat ADHD based off science, Dr Russell Barkley part of 2012 Burnett Lecture
videos.s: Short excerpt from Russell Barkley's 2012 Burnett Lecture on treating ADHD. He frames ADHD as a disorder of executive function and self-regulation and argues environments should compensate.
videos.w: Commenters see it as a shorter summary of Barkley's work, and one says it prompted them to schedule a full evaluation.

videos.t: Anki: Recommended Settings
videos.s: The AnKing explains recommended Anki settings for medical students.
videos.w: Commenters used it as the starting point for setting up their Anki decks.

videos.t: Important tips and tricks for IV cannulation!
videos.s: A video from ABCs of Anaesthesia with tips and step-by-step instruction for IV cannulation.
videos.w: A nurse recommends it as a visual resource with good tips and clear steps that match ED practice.

videos.t: War on Waste hospitals 2019
videos.s: A short film on a Brisbane hospitals recycling programme for operating theatre and anaesthesia waste, from a hospital sustainability group.
videos.w: Anesthesia commenters hold it up as a gold-standard example of hospital recycling.

videos.t: IV Insertion (Demonstrations)
videos.s: A demonstration video of IV insertion that covers catheter angle and advancing the needle.
videos.w: Commenters say it helped them with IV placement as new graduates, including one starting in the ER.

videos.t: Why Are American Health Care Costs So High?
videos.s: A vlogbrothers video analyzing why American health care costs are so high compared with other countries.
videos.w: Commenters call it a quick, clear breakdown showing that excess illness does not explain high US costs.

videos.t: More Cases From the Races - John Hinds
videos.s: A lecture by Dr. John Hinds, an anesthetist and intensivist who worked at Isle of Man motorcycle races, on trauma care and traumatic arrest at the track.
videos.w: Commenters describe Hinds as a legend and say the talk is worth watching, especially on managing traumatic arrest.

videos.t: Heart Murmurs | Locations, Maneuvers, Buzzwords
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video on heart murmurs covering their locations, maneuvers and buzzwords for USMLE.
videos.w: Students say it was passed around a school and left everyone confident on murmurs, with a simple and efficient explanation.

videos.t: Circle of Life cardiac resuscitation system
videos.s: London Ambulance Service video on its Circle of Life cardiac resuscitation system, including pit crew CPR.
videos.w: Commenters like its plain explanations for the public and its training-video style.

videos.t: Empathy: The Human Connection to Patient Care
videos.s: A short Cleveland Clinic film about empathy in patient care, showing the hidden stories of patients and caregivers.
videos.w: Viewers describe it as a moving short video that captures what empathy in patient care means.

videos.t: Chris Solomons Sudden Cardiac Arrest Rescue - BBC Helicopter Heroes
videos.s: BBC Helicopter Heroes segment on a witnessed sudden cardiac arrest with rapid CPR, defibrillation and return of circulation.
videos.w: Instructors show it in class because it displays agonal breathing and arm movement and prepares students better than staged training videos.

videos.t: A Waking Nightmare for COVID-19 Patients
videos.s: An Atlantic video in which COVID-19 patients recount their experiences of ICU delirium.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives perspective on ICU delirium and send it to people who shrug off wearing a mask.

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1035 - Paul Stamets
videos.s: Two-hour Joe Rogan Experience conversation with mycologist Paul Stamets on fungi, mycelium, bioremediation and medicinal mushrooms. It touches on Lion's Mane and psilocybin.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a fascinating, accessible introduction to the world of fungi.

videos.t: Anki: Suspend, Bury, Mark, Tags, & Decks
videos.s: The AnKing tutorial on suspending, burying, marking, tagging and organizing decks in Anki.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for using tags to find cards and unsuspend only a given tag.

videos.t: How to study for exams - Evidence-based revision tips
videos.s: Ali Abdaal reviews evidence-based revision techniques and why common methods like re-reading and note-taking work poorly.
videos.w: Commenters call it a must-watch for exam prep, especially for its active learning techniques.

videos.t: Neuroanatomy S1 E1: Intro to the Central Nervous System #neuroanatomy #science #medicine #brain
videos.s: The first episode of a UBC Medicine neuroanatomy series, introducing the central nervous system.
videos.w: Students list the UBC series among self-study resources they enjoyed.

videos.t: Stable Marriage Problem - Numberphile
videos.s: A Numberphile video on the Stable Marriage Problem, the mathematics behind the residency match algorithm.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows step by step what the match computer does and why rank lists work the way they do.

videos.t: Fasting vs. Eating Less: What's the Difference? (Science of Fasting)
videos.s: An explainer from the Joseph Everett channel on intermittent fasting versus simply eating less, drawing on published studies. It touches on appetite effects.
videos.w: Commenters say it uses studies to explain fasting science and summarizes a lot well, though not perfectly.

videos.t: Homeopathy Explained – Gentle Healing or Reckless Fraud?
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animated explainer on what homeopathy is, why it attracts people and why it has no active ingredient.
videos.w: Commenters send it to anyone unsure what homeopathic medicine actually is.

videos.t: selective attention test
videos.s: Daniel Simons' selective attention test, the video in which viewers count basketball passes and often miss a gorilla.
videos.w: Commenters use it to illustrate change blindness and how focus causes missed findings, including in neuroscience teaching.

videos.t: Personal Growth Series: Dr. William Dement on Healthy Sleep and Optimal Perfo...
videos.s: Google tech talk by sleep researcher William Dement on healthy sleep and performance. He argues that sleep debt must be fully repaid and describes the traits of healthy sleep.
videos.w: One commenter calls it the most useful source they found on sleep and says it changed their sleep habits.

videos.t: Anki: How to Avoid "Ease Hell" (aka doing too many cards)
videos.s: The AnKing video on how to avoid ease hell in Anki, where cards return too soon and review loads balloon.
videos.w: Users say it explains how pressing Hard causes ease hell and how to diagnose and reset ease.

videos.t: Welcome to the Hospital - A parody of Bo Burnham's "Welcome to the Internet"
videos.s: A resident-made music video parodying Bo Burnham's Welcome to the Internet, retold as a tour of hospital life.
videos.w: Commenters say it feels true to residency and love the Bo Burnham-style parody.

videos.t: Anki: How to Use Custom Filtered Decks
videos.s: The AnKing explains how to set up and use custom filtered decks in the Anki flashcard app.
videos.w: Commenters repeatedly point to it as the clear explanation of filtered decks.

videos.t: Dr. Cox - But Mostly It's The Getting By Thing - S02E06 - ALL RIGHTS TO NBC, ABC, and Doozer
videos.s: A clip from the TV comedy-drama Scrubs in which Dr. Cox talks about getting by after losing patients and keeping emotional distance.
videos.w: Healthcare workers call it a clip that captures grief and death on a unit and describe Cox's advice as essential.

videos.t: How to use Anki's Text-To-Speech (TTS)
videos.s: The AnKing video on setting up text-to-speech for Anki cards.
videos.w: Users say it helps them stay focused and get through reviews quicker, with one reporting more than double the speed.

videos.t: #NSDR (Non-Sleep Deep Rest) with Dr. Andrew Huberman
videos.s: A ten-minute guided Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR) relaxation session attributed to Andrew Huberman.
videos.w: Commenters in a nursing community recommend it as a short guided session to help with anxiety and rest.

videos.t: Integrative Biology 131 - Lecture 01: Organization of Body
videos.s: The first lecture of a Berkeley Integrative Biology 131 anatomy series, on the organization of the body.
videos.w: Commenters call the series a detailed, fantastic basic introduction to thinking about anatomy at undergraduate level.

videos.t: Autosomal Dominant Diseases Song || USMLE Mnemonic
videos.s: Dirty Medicine mnemonic song covering autosomal dominant diseases for USMLE.
videos.w: Students say the catchy songs cover most high-yield inheritance patterns, though not exhaustively.

videos.t: The Brachial Plexus explained
videos.s: An explainer on the brachial plexus, the nerve network of the shoulder and arm, from a channel that teaches it in a simplified way.
videos.w: Students describe it as a good foundation for the topic and say it shows how to draw the plexus simply, though commenters note minor errors.

videos.t: Vaccines and Autism: A Measured Response
videos.s: A long video essay from hbomberguy on vaccines and autism, anti-vaccine culture and the history of Andrew Wakefield.
videos.w: Commenters call it a well-researched, gripping account of anti-vax history, long and infuriating.

videos.t: Ain't the Way to Die | Eminem/Rihanna Remixed | Make Your End of Life Wishes Known
videos.s: A parody song by physician Zubin Damania (ZDoggMD), set to an Eminem and Rihanna track, urging people to make their end-of-life wishes known.
videos.w: Commenters call it a powerful message from a physician about end-of-life care and say it moves them each time.

videos.t: X-Linked Recessive Diseases Song || USMLE Mnemonic
videos.s: Dirty Medicine mnemonic song covering X-linked recessive diseases for USMLE.
videos.w: Students say the catchy songs cover most high-yield inheritance patterns, though not exhaustively.

videos.t: Dr. Jason Fung: Fasting as a Therapeutic Option for Weight Loss
videos.s: A talk by nephrologist Jason Fung on fasting as a therapeutic option for weight loss and obesity.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains intermittent fasting and argues calories in, calories out is not as simple as it seems.

videos.t: The Epidemic of Fake Disease
videos.s: Medlife Crisis video by cardiologist Rohin Francis on overdiagnosis and over-screening. It explains why detecting more disease does not always save more lives and covers harms such as unnecessary treatment.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for its coverage of over-testing and over-treatment, including breast cancer screening.

videos.t: The Complete Guide to Intravenous (IV) Cannulation LIVE DEMO | 2022 update
videos.s: An 18-minute live demonstration of intravenous cannulation by an anesthesiologist at ABCs of Anaesthesia, updated in 2022.
videos.w: Commenters say it taught IV principles well and helped a clinician when starting in the ED.

videos.t: Everything you think you know about addiction is wrong | Johann Hari | TED
videos.s: Johann Hari's TED talk arguing that addiction is driven largely by disconnection and environment rather than chemical hooks alone. He draws on experience with addicted relatives and on research and policy examples from around the world.
videos.w: Commenters call it their favorite addiction talk and repeat its point that the opposite of addiction is connection.

videos.t: Ken Jeong AHA Hands-Only CPR video
videos.s: An American Heart Association hands-only CPR video featuring Ken Jeong with a humorous take on chest compressions.
videos.w: Commenters say it is memorable and relevant, with actors that fit the times.

videos.t: Mindfulness with Jon Kabat-Zinn
videos.s: Hour-long Google talk in which Jon Kabat-Zinn introduces mindfulness and leads a guided meditation. It is pitched at newcomers.
videos.w: One commenter says it changed their perception of their own decision-making.

videos.t: USMLE Communications Questions
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video on USMLE communication and ethics questions.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best of several ethics videos and say it makes communication questions much easier.

videos.t: 30 Essential Ideas you should know about ADHD, 1A Intro, Chronic Developmental Disability
videos.s: First clip of Russell Barkley's 30 Essential Ideas about ADHD series, introducing ADHD as a chronic developmental disability.
videos.w: Commenters call Barkley's lectures a top researcher's best introduction to ADHD, stressing its emotional side.

videos.t: Cardiovascular | Fundamentals of Blood Pressure
videos.s: Ninja Nerd lecture on the fundamentals of blood pressure, with whiteboard diagrams.
videos.w: Commenters praise the plain-language explanations and excellent diagrams.

videos.t: What suicide is like
videos.s: Clip from a show in which a character describes what suicide is like.
videos.w: A commenter calls it the best description of suicide they have heard and says it helped them decide against ending their life.

videos.t: Why Some Diseases Only Traveled One Direction
videos.s: CGP Grey explains why European diseases devastated the Americas while few deadly diseases traveled the other way. He ties it to livestock domestication and dense cities, drawing on Guns, Germs and Steel.
videos.w: Commenters say it communicates the core of Guns, Germs and Steel on disease and conquest concisely.

videos.t: Anki: How To Update Decks with the Special Fields Add-on or Share Tags and Unsuspended Cards
videos.s: The AnKing video on updating decks with the Special Fields add-on while keeping your own edits and shared tags.
videos.w: Users say it solves the problem of updating a deck without overwriting their edits.

videos.t: Guided Wim Hof Method Breathing
videos.s: An 11-minute guided Wim Hof breathing session that uses an expanding and contracting bubble to pace the breath, over ambient sound.
videos.w: Commenters like it as an easy-to-follow guided exercise that includes safe-practice advice, and one calls it very valuable.

videos.t: Ringing in Ears Tinnitus Treatment
videos.s: Short promotional video demonstrating a head-thumping technique claimed to relieve tinnitus. Covering the ears and tapping the back of the head is said to silence the ringing temporarily.
videos.w: Commenters say the trick briefly silenced their tinnitus, and one calls it silence for the first time in decades.

videos.t: How to Make Stress Your Friend | Kelly McGonigal | TED
videos.s: A TED talk by health psychologist Kelly McGonigal on how people's beliefs about stress shape its effect on health, and how to relate to stress differently.
videos.w: Nursing students share it as advice for coping with stress and staying healthy.

videos.t: Dr. Oz and Nutritional Supplements: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A Last Week Tonight segment from John Oliver on Dr. Oz and the dietary supplement industry.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a good takedown of supplements and shows how easy it is to make a professional-looking one.

videos.t: DEF CON 25 - John Sotos - Genetic Diseases to Guide Digital Hacks of the Human Genome
videos.s: DEF CON 25 talk by physician and former Intel chief medical officer John Sotos on genetic diseases as exploitable weaknesses in the genome. He warns that CRISPR and related tools could make malicious genome hacks and targeted bioweapons feasible.
videos.w: Commenters describe it as captivating and somewhat frightening, and a good account of the risks of gene editing.

videos.t: It Was A Good Call Day (An Ice Cube "Good Day" Medical Parody)
videos.s: A ZDoggMD music video parodying Ice Cube's Good Day, retold as a good day on call for doctors.
videos.w: Commenters call it an epic and enjoyable medical parody.

videos.t: Orthopaedics vs Psychiatry
videos.s: A comedy sketch of a consult conversation between orthopaedics and psychiatry.
videos.w: Commenters call it a funny medical consult sketch that gets them every time.

videos.t: If money was no object, should you run every medical test?
videos.s: A Medlife Crisis video asking whether every medical test should be run if cost were no object.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for the statistics of testing without a clear indication and the false positives that result.

videos.t: Sterile Gloving Nursing Technique Steps | Don/Donning Sterile Gloves Tips
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN demonstrates the steps of sterile gloving technique.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows sterile gloving well and matches what experienced nurses teach.

videos.t: Why you can't compare Covid-19 vaccines
videos.s: A Vox explainer on why COVID-19 vaccines cannot be compared by their headline efficacy numbers.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains well how to compare efficacy against infection versus disease.

videos.t: Large (14G) cannula insertion technique - Live Demo
videos.s: A live demonstration of inserting a large 14G cannula from ABCs of Anaesthesia.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows that bevel size dictates how far to advance after the flash, and rewatch it.

videos.t: Getting On Season 1: Episode #1 Clip "Turd on Chair" (HBO)
videos.s: A clip from the first episode of the HBO series Getting On, a dark comedy set in a hospital extended-care unit.
videos.w: Nurses share clips from it because they consider the show unusually accurate about the profession.

videos.t: IV Insertion: Avoiding Common Mistakes
videos.s: A Practical Anesthesia Techniques video on common mistakes in IV insertion and why cannulation attempts fail.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains IV insertion well and helped them understand why they kept blowing veins.

videos.t: You Actually Share Your Brain With a Silent Stranger
videos.s: CGP Grey explains split-brain patients, where severing the corpus callosum lets the two hemispheres act independently, and uses it to explore two minds in one head.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a clear, entertaining explanation of the split-brain phenomenon from a strong educational channel.

videos.t: How to Use Anki for Rotations, Shelf Exams and Step 2
videos.s: The AnKing explains how to use Anki during clinical rotations, shelf exams and Step 2, including unlocking cards by rotation.
videos.w: Commenters repeatedly recommend it as the method that worked for them during clinicals.

videos.t: Dr. Jason Fung - 'Therapeutic Fasting - Solving the Two-Compartment Problem'
videos.s: Talk by nephrologist Jason Fung on therapeutic fasting as a treatment for obesity and type 2 diabetes. He frames it around the two-compartment problem of fat storage and insulin resistance.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an overview of Fung's work that addresses claims such as muscle loss during fasting.

videos.t: The Best Science-Based Minimalist Workout Plan (Under 45 Mins)
videos.s: A Jeff Nippard video presenting a science-based minimalist lifting program that takes under 45 minutes, two days a week.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a premade, simple routine for busy trainees to start with.

videos.t: TempleOS | Down the Rabbit Hole
videos.s: Fredrik Knudsen's 86-minute video documentary on Terry A. Davis, creator of TempleOS, tracing his work, his schizophrenia and his decline.
videos.w: Commenters call it the definitive account of Terry Davis's life and illness.

videos.t: Coronavirus Vaccines - An Introduction
videos.s: A JAMA Network introduction to the COVID-19 vaccine landscape, including the new vaccine technologies.
videos.w: Commenters call it a solid, digestible explanation of the vaccine candidates and why earlier approved vaccines did not use the new technology.

videos.t: How to Use a Controller For Anki
videos.s: The AnKing walkthrough of mapping a game controller to Anki to speed up reviews.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for controller setup, including with the Enjoyable app.

videos.t: How to Draw Out Anterior Chapman's Points for COMLEX
videos.s: A short video on drawing the anterior Chapman points for the COMLEX osteopathic exam.
videos.w: Students say the Chapman points are quick to memorize and to draw on scrap paper during the exam.

videos.t: FCVS Trick.Find out if you passed 8 hours early.
videos.s: A how-to video on creating an FSMB account and checking FCVS exam results online ahead of the official release.
videos.w: Commenters say it helped them check results for free instead of paying for a service.

videos.t: Dimensional Analysis for Nursing Pharmacology (example questions)
videos.s: A NURSING.com video teaching dimensional analysis for pharmacology dose calculations with example questions.
videos.w: Students say they practiced along with it repeatedly and found it an easy way into med math.

videos.t: Massive Pulmonary Embolus!
videos.s: Short surgical video of removing a massive straddle pulmonary embolism by thrombectomy.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows the huge clot at the end and call the resection fantastic.

videos.t: ENTRY LEVEL MASTERS in NURSING PROGRAMS | Worth it? Is BSN Better?
videos.s: Nurse Liz discusses entry-level master's programs in nursing and whether a BSN is better, including how education level relates to licensure.
videos.w: Commenters found it helpful for clarifying how nursing degrees map to licensure.

videos.t: Emma Holliday Surgery
videos.s: Emma Holliday's surgery clerkship review lecture.
videos.w: Students recommend it at the start of the block and before the shelf as a clinical overview, though it dates from around 2012.

videos.t: All doctors should know: legal dos (and don’ts) for emergency response outside the hospital
videos.s: An interview with an MD/JD medical ethicist on the legal dos and donts of emergency response outside the hospital, including Good Samaritan law.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a good overview of Good Samaritan protection and the duty to assist.

videos.t: Sunlight: Optimize Health and Immunity (Light Therapy and Melatonin)
videos.s: MedCram lecture of nearly two hours by Dr. Roger Seheult on sunlight beyond vitamin D. It covers the solar spectrum, circadian rhythm, melatonin and infrared light.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as an easily digestible doctor's review of the literature on sun exposure and health.

videos.t: A terrible guide to the terrible terminology of U.S. Health Insurance
videos.s: Comedic guide by Brian David Gilbert to the confusing terminology of US health insurance.
videos.w: Commenters call it a funny, easy-to-follow overview that is also useful and educational.

videos.t: The Poo in You - Constipation and Encopresis Educational Video
videos.s: An educational video from GIKids explaining what causes constipation and encopresis in children and why treatment has to be carried through fully.
videos.w: A commenter says anyone with constipation should watch it because it explains what is going on clearly.

videos.t: Cardiovascular | ECG Basics
videos.s: A Ninja Nerd lecture on ECG basics in a cardiovascular physiology series.
videos.w: Commenters say his ECG basics videos helped them and that the channel breaks down many medical subjects well.

videos.t: 24. Schizophrenia
videos.s: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford lecture on schizophrenia, covering its neurobiology, genetics and treatment with antipsychotics.
videos.w: Commenters call it a great breakdown of schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder and praise Sapolsky as a lecturer.

videos.t: Is Being Fat A Choice? (My Response)
videos.s: Jeff Nippard responds to the question of whether being fat is a choice, reviewing the literature on genetic and physiologic factors in obesity.
videos.w: Commenters call it a must-watch for people who say just eat less, and a fresh view on obesity.

videos.t: Crash Course Anatomy & Physiology Preview
videos.s: The preview video for CrashCourse's Anatomy and Physiology series, introducing the course.
videos.w: Students recommend the CrashCourse A&P series for reviewing anatomy and physiology.

videos.t: Verbal Judo: Diffusing Conflict Through Conversation
videos.s: Long Columbia Business School talk on verbal judo, defusing conflict through conversation.
videos.w: EMS and nursing commenters call it a must-watch model of calm de-escalation, even at 1.5 hours.

videos.t: First Responder Mental Heath is important
videos.s: Fire Department Chronicles video on first responder mental health and limited emotional reserves, with advice on coping after difficult events.
videos.w: Commenters say it applies to anyone and recommend everyone watch it.

videos.t: Is THIS How You Want To Die? | AMA 02
videos.s: A ZDoggMD AMA episode on resuscitation and end-of-life decisions, asking whether this is how you want to die.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a good explanation for families and show it to people choosing full code, to convey how futile resuscitation often is.

videos.t: The ECG Course - Introduction
videos.s: Introduction to The Resuscitationist's ECG course, a short-video series on ECG basics.
videos.w: Commenters advise watching a couple a day to build a solid base in rhythm interpretation.

videos.t: Ultimate Fluid and Electrolytes Crash Course: A Nursing School & NCLEX Review that is LIFE CHANGING
videos.ch: IV League Tutoring for Nursing Students
videos.s: IV League Tutoring's fluid and electrolytes review for nursing school and NCLEX, explaining electrolytes through pathophysiology.
videos.w: Students say it clicked for them and breaks electrolytes down to a foundational level.

videos.t: How to Study For Medical Surgical Nursing | Passing Med Surg in Nursing School
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN gives tips on how to study for medical-surgical nursing.
videos.w: Students say they found it extremely helpful as a plan for the semester.

videos.t: Arterial Blood Gas (ABG) Tic-Tac-Toe Examples
videos.s: survivenursing walks through examples of the tic-tac-toe method for interpreting arterial blood gases.
videos.w: Commenters call it the easiest way they have found to interpret acidosis and alkalosis on ABGs.

videos.t: How to Study for Nursing Fundamentals (Foundations) in Nursing School
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN gives tips on how to study for nursing fundamentals, with quizzes.
videos.w: Commenters call it an excellent review of concepts and note that she has several similar videos.

videos.t: Assessing Lung Sounds - Part 2
videos.s: Second part of a nursing-education lecture series on assessing lung sounds, continuing the walk-through by chest location and phase of breathing.
videos.w: Nursing students call it a clear, well-explained resource for learning lung sounds.

videos.t: State Medical Boards: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: Last Week Tonight segment on how US state medical boards license and discipline physicians.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good breakdown of state medical boards and a corrective to assumptions about how rarely licenses are removed.

videos.t: Assessing Lung Sounds - Part 1
videos.s: First part of a nursing-education lecture series on assessing lung sounds, organized by chest location and phase of breathing.
videos.w: Nursing students call it a clear, well-explained resource for learning lung sounds.

videos.t: That Mitchell and Webb Look: Homeopathic A&E
videos.s: A Mitchell and Webb comedy sketch set in a homeopathic emergency department.
videos.w: Commenters treat it as required viewing in any discussion of homeopathy.

videos.t: Tautology as Causality: Challenging the Assumptions That Underlie Our Expertise
videos.ch: UCSF Dept. of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
videos.s: A UCSF psychiatry grand rounds talk questioning how circular reasoning in diagnostic labels shapes psychiatric expertise.
videos.w: A commenter says all clinicians in mental health would benefit from this talk about how DSM labels can hold the field back.

videos.t: ABG - Arterial blood gas interpretation made simple in 8 minutes RN, LPN, LVN for NCLEX
videos.s: A SimpleNursing 8-minute walkthrough of reading arterial blood gases as acidosis or alkalosis, for NCLEX preparation.
videos.w: Students say the acid-base method explained well and finally made ABGs memorable.

videos.t: Cardiogenic Syncope - For the Faint of Heart | The Heart Course
videos.s: Amal Mattu lecture on cardiogenic syncope, covering causes of sudden cardiac death and ECG findings to look for.
videos.w: Commenters like it for the ECG pearls and for a lecturer they find very funny.

videos.t: Pulmonary Exam Demo (Strong Exam)
videos.s: Demonstration of a pulmonary physical examination from the Strong Medicine series, with focused auscultation.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for its evidence-based approach to the physical exam and call the series fantastic.

videos.t: Anki: How to Use Pre-made Decks Alongside Lecture- Med School Workflow
videos.s: Workflow video from The AnKing on using pre-made Anki decks alongside medical school lectures, including suspending and unsuspending cards by tag.
videos.w: Students name it the best video for learning how to use AnKing decks alongside classes.

videos.t: Normal sinus rhythm on an EKG | Circulatory System and Disease | NCLEX-RN | Khan Academy
videos.s: Khan Academy Medicine video explaining normal sinus rhythm on an EKG, part of a series on arrhythmias.
videos.w: A paramedic student says they learned more from this ten-minute video than from a day of medic school.

videos.t: Organ & Body Donations: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A Last Week Tonight segment on organ and body donation, covering where donations actually go, how donated bodies are used and sold, and problems in organ transplant programs.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a good episode on opaque systems that hide where donated bodies and organs end up.

videos.t: DNA animation (2002-2014) by Drew Berry and Etsuko Uno wehi.tv #ScienceArt
videos.s: Compilation of molecular animations of DNA replication and gene transcription by Drew Berry and Etsuko Uno at WEHI, with no narration. It shows the machinery inside cells at work.
videos.w: Commenters find it awe-inspiring and say seeing transcription as a mechanical process blew their minds.

videos.t: Medical embryology - Difficult concepts of early development.mp4
videos.s: A medical embryology lecture by Peter J Ward on the difficult concepts of early development, including gastrulation and neurulation.
videos.w: Students say it explains neurulation and gastrulation well and got them through introductory embryology.

videos.t: Doc (Clique medical school parody)
videos.s: A music video parody of Clique with lyrics about being a medical student, titled Doc.
videos.w: Commenters call it a clever, ridiculous pump-up song and the best of its kind.

videos.t: EKG or ECG Interpretation | Part 1/20
videos.s: Part 1 of Dr. Najeeb's 20-part lecture series on EKG interpretation.
videos.w: Learners say it makes EKG reading doable and detailed enough to help retention.

videos.t: The AnKing Deck- Getting Started and Updating
videos.s: The AnKing step-by-step walkthrough of getting started with and updating the AnKing deck.
videos.w: Users say it covers the required steps, including changing note type and keeping scheduling during an update.

videos.t: Sherwin Nuland: How electroshock therapy changed me
videos.s: A 2001 TED talk in which surgeon and author Sherwin Nuland tells how electroconvulsive therapy treated his severe depression.
videos.w: Commenters call it one of the best TED talks, a story of recovery and hope from a physician who was also a patient.

videos.t: "Why Zebras Don't Get Ulcers: Stress and Health" by Dr. Robert Sapolsky
videos.s: Robert Sapolsky lecture on how the body's stress response, evolved for short physical emergencies, harms long-term health when triggered by psychological stressors. It was given as the inaugural Fenton-Rhodes Lecture and runs under 90 minutes.
videos.w: Commenters call it a must-see on stress and health that is both informative and entertaining.

videos.t: The NEW Best Anki Settings 2024! New FSRS vs Anki default algorithm (SM-2)
videos.s: The AnKing video comparing the FSRS scheduler with the default SM-2 algorithm and recommending Anki settings.
videos.w: Users say it gives a detailed breakdown of the new scheduler and which settings to use.

videos.t: Anki: Customizing Card Styling (font, color, hints, etc)
videos.s: The AnKing tutorial on customizing Anki card styling, such as fonts, colors and hints.
videos.w: Users point to it for editing card templates, such as auto-showing hints or revealing resources on the back.

videos.t: I Genetically Engineered *MYSELF* to Fix Lactose Intolerance
videos.s: The Thought Emporium's host describes making and taking a DIY gene therapy for his own lactose intolerance. An AAV virus delivers DNA coding for the lactose-digesting enzyme, with help from a biohacker.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as an example of how accessible gene engineering has become and of the channel's biohacking content.

videos.t: mRNA Translation (Advanced)
videos.s: Short animation from the DNA Learning Center showing mRNA carrying a gene's message to the ribosome, where tRNA and codons assemble amino acids into a protein.
videos.w: Commenters say the visualization showed how tiny and intricate molecular processes are and blew their minds.

videos.t: Animations of unseeable biology | Drew Berry | TED
videos.s: Drew Berry's TEDxSydney talk showing scientifically accurate animations of molecular processes inside cells, such as DNA replication.
videos.w: Commenters say it gave them a greater appreciation for the many tiny protein machines in the body.

videos.t: Families sound alarm on medical transparency after deaths of their children  | NewsNation Now
videos.s: A NewsNation report on families calling for medical transparency after children died, with blame placed on midlevel providers.
videos.w: Commenters urge others to watch it as a news story on nurse practitioner practice and transparency.

videos.t: Michael Levin: The electrical blueprints that orchestrate life | TED

videos.s: Instructional video from InterAnest walking through endotracheal intubation step by step.
videos.w: Commenters say it suits people new to intubation and helps with landmark recognition through repetition.

videos.t: United Health Group Acquisition of Change Healthcare... Healthcare Data Goldmine
videos.s: A healthcare-finance explainer on UnitedHealth Group's acquisition of Change Healthcare and what it means for an insurer to own claims data. It also covers why the Change Healthcare hack reached so widely.
videos.w: Commenters call it a thorough explanation of who Change Healthcare is and why the hack affected so many providers.

videos.t: MASTER ECG/EKG INTERPRETATION: A Systematic Approach for 12 Lead ECG/EKGs
videos.s: A long Ninja Nerd lesson on reading 12-lead ECGs with a systematic approach.
videos.w: Students say it made ECGs understandable where textbooks did not, building on the earlier basics videos.

videos.t: Cardiologist’s scientific analysis of the Apple Watch
videos.s: A cardiologist from the Medlife Crisis channel gives a humorous but science-based take on the Apple Watch and its atrial fibrillation detection. He covers how wearable data can lead to extra tests and consults.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for people who risk becoming overly fixated on wearable readings.

videos.t: Shotgun Histology Introduction
videos.s: An introduction to the Shotgun Histology series of short normal-histology videos with key identification points and pathology slides.
videos.w: Students say the series helped with histology lab quizzes and catches you up quickly, though it is not comprehensive.

videos.t: CARING CORRUPTED - The Killing Nurses of The Third Reich
videos.s: A UTHealth Nursing documentary on nurses who took part in killing patients in 1930s and 1940s Germany.
videos.w: Commenters say all medical professionals should learn how unquestioning obedience slowly crept into health care.

videos.t: Cricolol
videos.s: A humorous conference speech by John Hinds arguing sarcastically against blind cricoid pressure during intubation.
videos.w: Commenters say it debunks the evidence for cricoid pressure better than any Cochrane review.

videos.t: Sebastian Seung: I am my connectome
videos.s: Sebastian Seung's TED talk on the connectome, the idea that the brain's wiring makes you who you are.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a favorite that sparked their interest in neuroscience.

videos.t: Chapman's Points (Anterior) For COMLEX Level I
videos.s: A COMLEX Level 1 review video covering the anterior Chapman's points used in osteopathic manipulative medicine.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for Chapman's points and suggest drawing the diagram while watching, though it runs long.

videos.t: The PROBLEM with Active Recall and Spaced Repetition (Truth Behind Studying Smarter)
videos.s: Justin Sung video on the limits of active recall and spaced repetition and why relational understanding matters.
videos.w: Commenters send it to learners who feel flashcards alone are not giving them real understanding.

videos.t: Our Patients Can Handle Reality: The Misuse of Insight to Justify Medication Treatment
videos.ch: UCSF Dept. of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
videos.s: A UCSF psychiatry grand rounds talk on how the concept of insight is used to justify medication treatment, with focus on early psychosis and coercion.
videos.w: A commenter says everyone working in mental health would benefit from watching it.

videos.t: Pancakes Every Day
videos.s: A satirical video from yourfriendalex that uses pancakes to illustrate the sheer volume of material in medical school.
videos.w: Commenters call it an accurate picture of why med school is hard through volume, and say it applies to nursing programs too.

videos.t: Anki: Image Occlusion Enhanced Add-on
videos.s: The AnKing explains the Image Occlusion Enhanced add-on for Anki, including fixing linked boxes.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a clear explanation of how to make and use image occlusion cards.

videos.t: What are those floaty things in your eye? - Michael Mauser
videos.s: A TED-Ed animation explaining what eye floaters are and related entoptic phenomena such as the blue field effect. It covers why they appear in your vision.
videos.w: Commenters call it a clear depiction of floaters that works for patients and professionals alike.

videos.t: ABG Interpretation: Simple Acid-Base Disorders (Lesson 3)
videos.s: A Strong Medicine lesson on interpreting arterial blood gases, covering simple acid-base disorders and their causes.
videos.w: Commenters call it a detailed lesson that goes from the basics to differentials and distinguishes acidemia from acidosis.

videos.t: Should You Get a Full Body Scan?
videos.s: A Medlife Crisis video on whether to get a full body scan and the consumer screening scans sold directly to the public.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for showing how overtesting and full body scans can harm patients.

videos.t: Stages of Labor Nursing OB for Nursing Students | Stages of Labour NCLEX Explained Video Lecture
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN lecture on the stages of labor for nursing OB courses and NCLEX preparation.
videos.w: Commenters call it an amazing short summary of labor and delivery that helped them.

videos.t: Dr. Gabor Maté — Trauma, Addiction, Ayahuasca, and More
videos.s: Long Tim Ferriss podcast interview with physician Gabor Mate on trauma, addiction, depression, ADHD and ayahuasca. Mate explains how childhood stress and emotional pain underlie many addictions and illnesses.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an honest look at the causes and mechanisms of addiction and at the effects of stress on children.

videos.t: On USMLE for DOs - and the future of the NBOME
videos.s: A Sheriff of Sodium video on USMLE for osteopathic students, the COMLEX exam and the future of the NBOME.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for why the COMLEX pass threshold differs and for criticism of the NBOME and DO school finances.

videos.t: The Inner Life of the Cell Animation
videos.s: Award-winning 3D animation by XVIVO for Harvard's BioVisions showing the molecular machinery inside a cell as a white blood cell responds to a stimulus.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a striking visualization of protein machines working inside cells.

videos.t: Jack Szostak (Harvard/HHMI) Part 1: The Origin of Cellular Life on Earth
videos.s: Jack Szostak lecture on how cellular life could have arisen from chemistry on the early Earth. It is the first part of a series on protocells and the RNA world.
videos.w: Commenters say it outlines well how life might have arisen from simple molecules.

videos.t: How To Survive Medical School | A Doctor's UNCENSORED TRUTH
videos.s: A video by Zubin giving a doctor's candid advice on surviving medical school, with study tips.
videos.w: One commenter calls it the most high-yield video they watched in medical school, and another says it applies to nursing students too.

videos.t: The NRMP Residency Match Algorithm [UndergroundMed]
videos.s: An UndergroundMed explainer of the NRMP residency match algorithm and how ranking and matching work.
videos.w: Commenters say it makes ranking and matching crystal clear.

videos.t: Your Brain Thinks Your Whole Home Is One Room
videos.s: A CGP Grey video on how living in one place during lockdown blurs the mind's sense of separate spaces and what to do about it.
videos.w: Commenters say the attitude it describes helped them through the pandemic.

videos.t: The Applicant’s Guide to Strategic Preference Signaling (2023)
videos.s: Sheriff of Sodium guide to strategic preference signaling in residency applications, using match cycle data.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for its argument for listing many geographic regions when signaling.

videos.t: Coronavirus Epidemic Update 34: US Cases Surge, Chloroquine & Zinc Treatment Combo, Italy Lockdown
videos.s: A MedCram early-pandemic update on COVID-19 cases, Italy's lockdown and the proposed chloroquine and zinc combination.
videos.w: Commenters like its well-researched explanation of chloroquine as a zinc ionophore, with primary sources in the description.

videos.t: Let's talk about nurses and a message to hospital administrators....
videos.s: A commentary video from the channel Belle of the Ranch on a legislative issue affecting nurses, with a message aimed at hospital administrators.
videos.w: Commenters call it a great summary of the legislation and credit the host with speaking up for nurses.

videos.t: The shocking centre of the COVID-19 crisis
videos.s: A Sky News report from inside a hospital at the center of the COVID-19 crisis, showing frontline care.
videos.w: Health professionals call it eye-opening and share it to show what is coming for nurses working without enough PPE.

videos.t: My Thoughts On The United Healthcare CEO Murder
videos.s: Dr. Glaucomflecken gives his take on the murder of the UnitedHealthcare CEO and what it says about US healthcare.
videos.w: Nurses say he best explains what healthcare workers already know to be true.

videos.t: Developmental (Pediatric) Milestones (IN UNDER 5 MINUTES)
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video summarizing pediatric developmental milestones in under five minutes using mnemonics.
videos.w: Commenters say the mnemonics are good and covered the basics and major milestones sufficiently.

videos.t: The Roots of Your Profits - Dr Elaine Ingham, Soil Microbiologist, Founder of Soil Foodweb Inc
videos.s: Soil microbiologist Elaine Ingham speaks at the Oxford Real Farming Conference on how soil organisms cycle nutrients and why pesticides and fertilizers harm soil life.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as an explanation of how soil microbes make minerals available and how pesticides damage them.

videos.t: Stable Marriage Problem (the math bit)
videos.s: The follow-up Numberphile video on the maths of the Stable Marriage Problem, including the theorem behind the match algorithm.
videos.w: Commenters say the part 2 theorem clears up confusion about how the Match works.

videos.t: How to Use Pre-Made Decks on ANKI (feat. ZANKI: The Ultimate FREE, USMLE Resource)
videos.s: Prerak Juthani video on using pre-made Anki decks, featuring the free Zanki deck.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for searching keywords, moving cards between decks and using premade decks selectively.

videos.t: Bret Weinstein on "The Portal" (w/ host Eric Weinstein), Ep. #019 - The Prediction and the DISC.
videos.s: Long Portal podcast episode in which Bret Weinstein tells Eric Weinstein the story of his lab mice telomere work, the prediction behind it and what it means for science and aging.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as the full account of the lab mice telomere claims and the changed breeding protocols.

videos.t: Anki Tutorial: Using Tags to Make a Filtered Deck
videos.s: Anki tutorial on tagging cards and building a filtered deck by tag.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for how to find and study tagged cards in Anki.

videos.t: Statins, Fibrates, Niacin, etc. - Easy Pharm for USMLE Step 1
videos.s: Pharm 450 visual mnemonic video on lipid-lowering drugs such as statins, fibrates and niacin.
videos.w: Students say it gives a clearer picture of lipid therapy than the Sketchy section.

videos.t: Ethics (USMLE/COMLEX Practice Questions)
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video of USMLE and COMLEX practice questions on medical ethics and communication.
videos.w: Students say watching it once or twice left them prepared, as exam questions closely matched its content.

videos.t: Stress, Portrait of a Killer - Full Documentary (2008)
videos.s: A 2008 documentary on the effects of chronic stress on the body, featuring Robert Sapolsky and using a baboon troop as the central example.
videos.w: Commenters name it as a favorite Sapolsky video and one they enjoyed watching for school.

videos.t: Anki: The Evolution of Med School Decks (Zanki, Lightyear, etc)
videos.s: The AnKing video tracing the evolution of medical school Anki decks such as Zanki and Lightyear.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for understanding where the AnKing and Lightyear decks came from.

videos.t: Master USMLE®️ Questions and crush your Step 1 exam with these Strategies
videos.s: An AMBOSS video on strategies for USMLE Step 1 questions, dissecting board-style questions step by step.
videos.w: Commenters call it a very helpful basic overview that puts question strategy in context.

videos.t: USMLE STEP 1 BIOSTATISTICS: DRUG ADS, ABSTRACT (PART 1)
videos.s: Randy Neil's USMLE Step 1 video on biostatistics, covering drug ads and how to approach abstract-based questions.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives a formulated approach to abstract questions and shows what kinds of drug ads appear.

videos.t: Guide to Anki Intervals and Learning Steps
videos.s: A guide to configuring Anki intervals and learning steps for medical school study.
videos.w: Students say the settings made their review load manageable while keeping up with past material.

videos.t: Evo-Devo (Despacito Biology Parody) | A Capella Science
videos.s: A Capella Science parody of Despacito that sings through evolutionary developmental biology, including body-axis genes and dormant snake leg DNA. It runs about four minutes.
videos.w: Commenters like it as a quick, standalone summary of how a single cell becomes a body.

videos.t: Bret Weinstein and Yuri Deigin: Did Covid-19 leak From a Lab?
videos.s: Bret Weinstein and Yuri Deigin discuss the evidence for the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 leaked from a lab, including the furin cleavage site and gain-of-function research.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a case for the lab leak hypothesis from a virologist who also finds it plausible.

videos.t: Is olive oil safe at high heat? Does it taste bad?
videos.s: Adam Ragusea examines whether olive oil is unsafe for high-heat cooking and whether it tastes bad when heated. He cites studies on its stability and says smoke-point worries are overblown.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a well-cited debunking of the myth that olive oil is unsafe at high heat.

videos.t: Anki: ReMemorize
videos.s: The AnKing video explaining the ReMemorize add-on for skipping days and handling review backlogs.
videos.w: Users call it a fantastic explanation of what to do with a backlog.

videos.t: Intro to Anki & The AnKing Step Deck & AnkiHub | Medical School Anki Beginner Tutorial | AnKing v12
videos.s: The AnKing beginner tutorial on Anki, the AnKing step deck and AnkiHub for medical school.
videos.w: Commenters say the free videos are worth watching, including the segment on downloading from AnkiHub and protecting fields.

videos.t: Anki Settings: A Complete Guide and Recommended Settings For Medical School
videos.s: Zach Highley guide to Anki settings, with recommended settings for medical school.
videos.w: Commenters say it answers every question about setting up Anki.

videos.t: Lysosomal Storage Diseases in Less Than 15 Minutes
videos.s: Video covering lysosomal storage diseases with mnemonics in under 15 minutes.
videos.w: Students call it an entertaining, Sketchy-style way to remember lysosomal storage diseases.

videos.t: HyGuru | USMLE Step 1: 100 Concepts in Gross Anatomy
videos.s: A HyGuru review of 100 gross anatomy concepts for USMLE Step 1, mostly musculoskeletal.
videos.w: Students used it the day before the exam and say it covers most of the anatomy and breaks it down nicely.

videos.t: My Caribbean Medical School Experience | This Was Unexpected...
videos.s: Kevin Jubbal, M.D. gives a critical account of attending a Caribbean medical school and its outcomes.
videos.w: Students call it an honest takedown of Caribbean schools, with a speaker who tells the truth about results.

videos.t: Divine Intervention Episode 29 Comprehensive 3rd Year NBME Medicine Shelf Review Session 1
videos.s: A Divine Intervention podcast episode, session 1 of a comprehensive third-year internal medicine shelf review.
videos.w: Commenters say the medicine series helped solidify shaky concepts and suggest this one shows what the rest are like.

videos.t: Cyclists' hearts: can you be so fit that you die?
videos.s: Medlife Crisis examines why some elite endurance athletes die in their sleep, covering extremely slow heart rates and performance-enhancing drugs that thicken blood. It uses cyclist Marco Pantani as an example.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a good video on athlete heart and the risks of extreme fitness and doping.

videos.t: Aortic Stenosis - Heart Sounds - MEDZCOOL
videos.s: A Medzcool video on the heart sounds of aortic stenosis, from a series that shows murmurs on screen while playing the sound.
videos.w: Commenters say the channel helped them a lot and praise its on-screen graphics of the murmurs.

videos.t: The Gunner Song ft. Harvard Medical School
videos.s: The Gunner Song, a music video parody by Harvard Medical School students about the overly competitive classmate.
videos.w: Commenters call it a solid, must-watch med school music video with some funny bits.

videos.t: High Yield Internal Medicine Review for Step 2 CK & Shelf Exam
videos.s: A high-yield internal medicine review for Step 2 CK and the shelf exam by Doctor High Yield.
videos.w: A student says it directly covered questions that appeared on their exam.

videos.t: High Yield Psychiatry Review for Step 2 CK & Shelf Exam
videos.s: A Doctor High Yield psychiatry review for the Step 2 CK and shelf exam.
videos.w: Commenters call it a high-yield pre-exam psychiatry review, and one says it raised their psychiatry scores.

videos.t: How to Use Anki Effectively - Flash Card Basics for Pre-Med and Med Students [Part 1]
videos.s: Part 1 of a Med School Insiders series on using Anki effectively, covering flashcard basics such as cloze deletion and image occlusion.
videos.w: Commenters call it easily the best tutorial and a helpful series from a med-student channel.

videos.t: High Yield Family Medicine Review for Step 2 CK & Shelf Exam
videos.s: Doctor High Yield's rapid-fire family medicine review for the Step 2 CK and shelf exam.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good rapid-fire shelf review that is still relevant despite its age.
