videos.t: The Backwards Brain Bicycle - Smarter Every Day 133
videos.s: Destin of Smarter Every Day learns to ride a bicycle with reversed steering, which takes about eight months, and compares it with how his young son learned far faster. It illustrates knowledge versus understanding and brain plasticity in adults versus children.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a fascinating demonstration of how brains cling to learned habits and how plasticity differs between adults and children.

videos.t: THE STROKE CHART w/ examples- MINUTES TO WIN IT! (USMLE)
videos.s: AshimaTalks video on the stroke chart with examples for lesion localization, under ten minutes.
videos.w: Students say it helped with exam questions and is all they need for strokes.

videos.t: Normal Heart Sounds - MEDZCOOL
videos.s: A Medzcool video on normal heart sounds, part of a playlist for seeing and hearing each murmur.
videos.w: Commenters call the playlist all you need for heart sounds and helpful for Step 1 and Step 2.

videos.t: How To REALLY Use Anki (USMLE Prep)
videos.s: Video by a physician on how to use Anki for USMLE prep, covering organization and cloze deletions.
videos.w: Students call it the source of the best Anki tips and a good place to learn the basics.

videos.t: Brachial Plexus- How to draw it well in less than 20 seconds
videos.s: A Med School Made Easy shorthand method for drawing the brachial plexus quickly.
videos.w: Students call it the nicest shorthand drawing video for learning the roots and nerves.

videos.t: 40 High Yield Images for USMLE (CT, XRay, Histology)
videos.s: Dirty Medicine video of 40 high-yield CT, x-ray and histology images for USMLE.
videos.w: Students say it covers most of the high-yield images and helped them answer a question on the real exam.

videos.t: The paradox of choice | Barry Schwartz | TED
videos.s: Barry Schwartz's TED talk on the paradox of choice, arguing that more options can lower satisfaction.
videos.w: Students cite it for choosing a specialty: pick one and commit rather than worry about the alternatives.

videos.t: Autosomal Recessive Disease Song
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine mnemonic song for autosomal recessive inheritance, part of a series of songs on inheritance patterns.
videos.w: Commenters say the songs are catchy, not comprehensive, and good for quickly memorizing inheritance patterns.

videos.t: Sketchy Anki Instructions
videos.s: Instructions from Dr Sultan Pepper on using his Sketchy Anki deck, including hierarchical tags.
videos.w: Commenters call the deck the best-put-together Sketchy deck and say to follow the video to use it correctly.

videos.t: USMLE STEP 1: COMMUNICATION (PATIENT-CENTERED) w/ Questions
videos.s: A Randy Neil video on patient-centered communication for USMLE Step 1, with practice questions.
videos.w: Students say his communication videos are good and that watching them paid off on the exam.

videos.t: Cross sectional and imaging anatomy of the abdomen
videos.s: A Human Anatomy Education video walking through abdominal CT slices alongside matching cross-sectional anatomy.
videos.w: Students say it goes through each CT cut against the corresponding cross section and shows how CT displays slices.

videos.t: A Basic, Simplified Approach to the Dizzy Patient Part 1
videos.s: Peter Johns video presenting a basic, simplified approach to the dizzy patient, part 1.
videos.w: Commenters recommend his videos for approaching dizziness.

videos.t: Introduction to Intubation - 01 - Approach: Sequence
videos.s: First video in an Introduction to Intubation series by Eric Shappell covering approaches, devices and sequences.
videos.w: Commenters call it a quick, simple rundown of intubation styles and sequences.

videos.t: Connectomics: Jeff Lichtman at TEDxCaltech
videos.s: A TEDx talk by Jeff Lichtman on connectomics, the mapping of the brain's neural connections, with images of those connections.
videos.w: Shared by a student whose neurobiology class showed it, who found the images of the brain's connections breath-taking.

videos.t: Motivational interviewing in brief consultations | BMJ Learning
videos.s: A BMJ Learning video demonstrating motivational interviewing in brief consultations, with an example of talking about weight.
videos.w: Commenters like it as a good example of MI, partly because one of its creators is involved.

videos.t: How To Unionize Your Workplace
videos.s: A how-to video on organizing a union at your workplace, recommended in a healthcare worker context.
videos.w: Commenters say it gets everyone up to speed on how unionizing works.

videos.t: Fluent Aphasia (Wernicke's Aphasia)
videos.s: A short clip showing a patient with fluent aphasia, the kind associated with Wernicke's area.
videos.w: Students say it is a decent example of what Wernicke's aphasia sounds like.

videos.t: Half Somersault Maneuver to Treat BPPV Vertigo
videos.s: An ENT clinic demonstration of the half somersault (Foster) maneuver for treating BPPV vertigo.
videos.w: A clinician says it is easier for patients than other maneuvers and seems just as effective.

videos.t: The Science & Process of Healing From Grief
videos.s: An Andrew Huberman podcast episode on the science and process of healing from grief, framed through neuroscience.
videos.w: Commenters offer it to someone grieving as an episode that may bring some solace.

videos.t: John Hinds Defends Prehospital Direct Laryngoscopy
videos.s: Talk by John Hinds defending prehospital direct laryngoscopy and presenting the case against routine intubation.
videos.w: A commenter says Hinds argues the case far better than they can.

videos.t: Outline the Stems for Anesthesia Oral Boards
videos.s: Short teaching video by an anesthesiology attending on how to outline stems for the anesthesia oral boards.
videos.w: Residents say it gave them an organized way to start each stem so they do not freeze on exam day.

videos.t: Living Arrhythmias with soundtrack
videos.s: A playful video in which people act out cardiac arrhythmias to a soundtrack, using arms as atria and legs as ventricles.
videos.w: Commenters call it an old but surprisingly accurate and fun visualization of cardiac rhythm problems.

videos.t: Sundance Film Festival (2014) - Alive Inside: A Story Of Music & Memory Featurette - Documentary HD
videos.s: Featurette from the documentary Alive Inside about music therapy for people with dementia.
videos.w: Used in training and called powerful by commenters.

videos.t: Cells at Work! English Dub Promotional Video
videos.s: A promotional trailer for the English dub of Cells at Work!, an anime that portrays the body's cells as characters.
videos.w: Commenters recommend the show as a fun and fairly educational anime about the body.

videos.t: Hematology- Making a Peripheral Blood Smear
videos.s: A lab demonstration of making a peripheral blood smear slide for hematology.
videos.w: Commenters call the technique shown the easiest and best way to make a slide.

videos.t: mRNA Vaccines - Layman’s version (Pfizer/Moderna COVID-19 vaccines), plus some FAQs, Animation.
videos.s: An Alila Medical Media animation explaining how the Pfizer and Moderna mRNA COVID-19 vaccines work, with some FAQs.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best explainer they found specifically on mRNA vaccines, though it is jargon-heavy.

videos.t: Run for your life! At a comfortable pace, and not too far: James O'Keefe at TEDxUMKC
videos.s: TEDx talk by cardiologist and lifelong runner James O'Keefe arguing that moderate running gives the best longevity benefit while extreme endurance training can damage the heart.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as an explanation of how extreme exercise can scar the heart, and one says they think about it often.

videos.t: The Unfixed Brain
videos.s: University of Utah Neuroscience Initiative video examining an unfixed human brain.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good neuroscience refresher that shows how malleable the brain is.

videos.t: Does Wellbutrin Make Anxiety Worse? Wellbutrin For Anxiety Disorders (Bupropion And Anxiety)
videos.s: A Psychofarm video on whether bupropion (Wellbutrin) worsens anxiety, reviewing the evidence on its effect compared with SSRIs.
videos.w: Commenters call it a helpful, great video on bupropion and anxiety.

videos.t: 6 ways mushrooms can save the world | Paul Stamets | TED
videos.s: Mycologist Paul Stamets gives an 18-minute TED talk on six ways mycelium and fungi could help save the world, including environmental cleanup.
videos.w: Commenters call it a brilliant talk on the world-changing potential of fungi research.

videos.t: Divide and Conquer
videos.s: A Dr. Glaucomflecken comedy sketch about health care professions fighting each other instead of cooperating.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a hilarious, too-close-to-home take on divide and conquer among clinicians.

videos.t: How to insert big cannulas - the lift and advance technique Dr Hugh Reid Newcastle NSW
videos.s: Demonstration by an anesthetist of a lift-and-advance technique for inserting large-bore IV cannulas.
videos.w: Commenters list it among IV insertion videos they rewatch and call out a tip rarely mentioned elsewhere.

videos.t: Fat Chance: Fructose 2.0
videos.s: Robert Lustig of UCSF updates his sugar talk, arguing that fructose and processed foods drive obesity and metabolic syndrome through endocrine effects. It is a roughly 90-minute university lecture.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it, alongside his other talk, as an explanation of how sugar and hormones drive obesity.

videos.t: The $100 Billion Dollar Ingredient making your Food Toxic
videos.s: What I've Learned video arguing that industrial seed and vegetable oils have displaced saturated fats and harmed health. It covers the history of vegetable oils, the American Heart Association's role and rising consumption.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as information on seed oils and the omega-6 to omega-3 ratio that led them to change which fats they eat.

videos.t: Ortho Admits Patient To Medicine
videos.s: A Dr. Glaucomflecken comedy sketch about an orthopedic surgeon admitting a patient to the medicine service.
videos.w: Commenters say his satire makes frustrating consult interactions easier to bear.

videos.t: Getting On Season 1: Episode #1 Clip "Language Barrier" (HBO)
videos.s: A scene from the HBO comedy Getting On, set in a hospital geriatric ward, showing nurses dealing with a language barrier.
videos.w: Commenters say the comedy is very true to life for clinicians and like the language line scene.

videos.t: Respiratory | Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve
videos.s: A Ninja Nerd lecture on the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve and the factors that shift it left or right.
videos.w: Commenters call it a helpful lecture that shows the curve shifts simply.

videos.t: Adam Ruins Everything - You Probably Have Herpes and That's Okay (Excerpt)
videos.s: A truTV Adam Ruins Everything excerpt arguing that herpes is very common and should not carry the stigma it does.
videos.w: A clinician says they tell patients to watch it because it destigmatizes herpes and counters sex-ed fear mongering.

videos.t: Opioids: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: Last Week Tonight segment on the US opioid epidemic, tracing how prescription painkillers fed addiction and heroin use. It is the first of three episodes the show devoted to the crisis.
videos.w: Commenters say it compiles an impressive amount of testimony and facts on how prescription opioids lead to heroin.

videos.t: A Man Took Dinitrophenol DNP To "Lose Weight" And This Happened
videos.s: A Chubbyemu case video about a man who took dinitrophenol (DNP) to lose weight and the toxicity that followed.
videos.w: Commenters call it an entertaining cautionary case study of DNP for laypeople.

videos.t: Scrub pants drawstring technique
videos.s: Short practical video showing a different way to tie scrub pants drawstrings.
videos.w: A commenter says they have tied their scrubs this way ever since.

videos.t: Biostatistics Tutorial Full course for Beginners to Experts
videos.s: Long beginner-to-advanced course on biostatistics from the Academic Lesson channel.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives a broad overview with some depth and covers most of the biostatistics one needs.

videos.t: Pulmonary Artery Catheter Insertion.mp4
videos.s: Procedure video showing pulmonary artery catheter insertion by Barry Bloom.
videos.w: Commenters found it helpful for syringe handling and aspiration while advancing the needle and for central line landmark technique.

videos.t: exercises for tendinitis (tendonitis) and carpal tunnel (cps)
videos.s: Short video from a percussion teacher with stretching and hand exercises for preventing and easing tendinitis and carpal tunnel syndrome, shown to him by a doctor.
videos.w: Commenters say the daily exercises relieved their hand and wrist pain and repetitive strain problems.

videos.t: A Boy Ate 150 Gummy Vitamins For Breakfast. This Is What Happened To His Bones.
videos.s: A Chubbyemu case video about a boy who ate 150 gummy vitamins and developed vitamin D toxicity with high calcium.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a case showing the danger of excess vitamin intake.

videos.t: Vasopressors Explained Clearly: Norepinephrine, Epinephrine, Vasopressin, Dobutamine...
videos.s: A MedCram lecture explaining the main vasopressors and inotropes, including norepinephrine, epinephrine, vasopressin and dobutamine.
videos.w: Commenters call it a simple foundation for nurses new to the ICU.

videos.t: A Toddler Played With His Cat. This Is What Happened To His Brain.
videos.s: Chubbyemu tells a dramatized case of a toddler with fever and brain symptoms, tracing it to toxoplasmosis encephalitis and explaining the disease step by step.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good case study on toxoplasmosis.

videos.t: RSA ANIMATE: The Divided Brain
videos.s: RSA Animate summary of Iain McGilchrist's lecture on the divided brain, arguing that the two hemispheres attend to the world differently and that this has shaped culture and society.
videos.w: Commenters call it an excellent animated introduction to McGilchrist's thesis on the hemispheres.

videos.t: Doctor vs PA vs NP | Which is Right for You?
videos.s: A Med School Insiders video comparing the doctor, PA and NP career paths and which fits you.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for Dr. Jubbals pointed take on NP and PA training versus physician training.

videos.t: How to Learn Faster with the Feynman Technique (Example Included)
videos.s: Thomas Frank video explaining the Feynman technique for learning with a worked example.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for learning by understanding and teaching rather than memorizing.

videos.t: Doctor's Reaction to: "Nurses Play Cards" | Wednesday Checkup
videos.s: An episode of Doctor Mike's Wednesday Checkup in which he reacts to a senator's comment that nurses play cards, and gives a physician's view of it.
videos.w: Nurses say it gave fair context and good insight on the senator's remarks about their profession.

videos.t: Arterial Blood Gas | ABGs Made Easy for Nurses | Tic Tac Toe Method
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN teaches arterial blood gas interpretation with the tic-tac-toe method, aimed at nursing students.
videos.w: Students say her videos made the material clear after classroom teaching left them confused.

videos.t: Orthopedics vs Anesthesia
videos.s: A comedy sketch of a conversation between orthopedics and anesthesia, a variant of the classic specialty-rivalry skit.
videos.w: Commenters call it a classic whose quotes stay with medical students.

videos.t: The treatment of cardiac arrest (1958)
videos.s: A 1958 Wellcome Library film about the treatment of cardiac arrest, showing how resuscitation was done in the operating room at the time.
videos.w: Commenters find it a fascinating look at how cardiac resuscitation used to work, including what shocked VFib looks like.

videos.t: The Brachial Plexus- Animated Review [HD]
videos.s: An animated review of the brachial plexus from FSU's medical media team, about seven minutes long.
videos.w: First-year students use it as a quick way to learn what the brachial plexus is.

videos.t: How to study for exams - The Retrospective Revision Timetable
videos.s: Ali Abdaal explains the retrospective revision timetable, an exam-prep method built around active recall.
videos.w: Commenters say they use it alongside school lectures to plan exam revision.

videos.t: Endocrine System, Part 1 - Glands & Hormones: Crash Course Anatomy & Physiology #23
videos.s: A CrashCourse Anatomy and Physiology episode on the endocrine system, covering glands and hormones.
videos.w: Students recommend the CrashCourse A&P series as awesome for review.

videos.t: The Neuroscience of Memory - Eleanor Maguire
videos.s: A Royal Institution lecture by Eleanor Maguire on the neuroscience of memory, covering the hippocampus, scene construction and boundary extension.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a fascinating watch for anyone writing about memory or interested in scene construction.

videos.t: How to Read Textbooks Efficiently in College or Nursing School | Nursing School Study Tips (Part 5)
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN explains how to read textbooks efficiently, with a skim-reading method, part 5 of a nursing school study tips series.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a different method for skim reading a nursing textbook.

videos.t: Hubel & Wiesel - Cortical Neuron - V1
videos.s: A video of the Hubel and Wiesel experiments mapping receptive fields of cortical neurons in the visual cortex.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for a basic understanding of edge detection in V1.

videos.t: 10. Introduction to Neuroscience I
videos.s: A Stanford lecture from Robert Sapolsky's behavioral biology series, an introduction to neuroscience that starts with neurons and long-term potentiation.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a strong starting point and a great introductory neuroscience lecture.

videos.t: I've No More F***s To Give!
videos.s: A comic song about running out of patience, which commenters read as being about medical school.
videos.w: Commenters say it feels painfully real for medical school and is relatable if you are burned out.

videos.t: Australian Health Care
videos.s: A short Healthcare Triage video on how the Australian health care system works.
videos.w: Commenters like it as a brief policy overview, part of a series comparing national health systems.

videos.t: Is Medical Error Really the 3rd Highest Cause of Death?
videos.s: A Medlife Crisis video examining the claim that medical error is the third leading cause of death in the US.
videos.w: Commenters call it well researched, tracing how the statistic originated and why media over-reported it.

videos.t: Where Do Medical Words Come From?
videos.s: A Medlife Crisis video on where medical terminology comes from and why Latin is less helpful than people assume.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a clear explanation of the origins of medical words.

videos.t: Noxious or Nociceptive Stimuli in Neurologic Evaluations
videos.s: Larry Mellick video on noxious stimuli in neurologic evaluation, including techniques for telling nonepileptic from epileptic seizures.
videos.w: Commenters say it goes over pseudoseizures and epileptic seizures and ways to identify them.

videos.t: Desired Over Have Dosage Calculations for Nursing Students and Nurses NCLEX
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN teaches the desired-over-have method of dosage calculation for nursing students.
videos.w: Commenters say it makes the most sense of the methods and helped them pass dosage tests.

videos.t: ABGs Made Easy for Nurses w/ Tic Tac Toe Method for Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation
videos.s: RegisteredNurseRN teaches arterial blood gas interpretation with the tic-tac-toe method for nursing students.
videos.w: Students say the tic-tac-toe boards helped a great deal and made ABGs easy once learned.

videos.t: How to Improve Your Surgical Mask Fit-- Covid-19
videos.s: A physician shows a way to improve the fit and seal of a regular surgical mask during the COVID-19 pandemic.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a fold trick that gives a better seal on a surgical mask.

videos.t: The PERFECT Home Workout (Sets and Reps Included)
videos.s: An ATHLEAN-X video laying out a home workout with sets and reps.
videos.w: A commenter offers it for home exercise ideas, noting the presenter talks a lot and you can skip around.

videos.t: Patients at Risk: The Rise of the Nurse Practitioner and Physician Assistant in Healthcare
videos.s: A documentary-style talk from AAPS Video arguing against the expansion of nurse practitioners and physician assistants, reviewing studies on independent practice.
videos.w: A commenter notes it goes through the studies for and against NP independent practice.

videos.t: Cardiac Arrhythmias, Animation
videos.s: Alila Medical Media animation covering how cardiac arrhythmias arise, including ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation, and how they relate to the rhythm on a monitor.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a good overview of ventricular arrhythmias that links heart movement to the monitor trace.

videos.t: EKG Interpretation for Nurses (Next-Gen NCLEX Prep & Clinical Practice)
videos.s: A MINT Nursing lesson on EKG interpretation for nurses, aimed at NCLEX and clinical practice.
videos.w: Students say it helped them with EKG interpretation in a critical care class.

videos.t: how is prangent formed
videos.s: A comedy compilation of real Yahoo Answers pregnancy questions read aloud.
videos.w: Healthcare workers call it a true gem and an all-time favorite for its ridiculous questions about pregnancy.

videos.t: orthopedia vs anesthesia (orthopaedics, anaesthetics conversation)
videos.s: A comedy sketch of an orthopedics and anesthesia phone conversation, a staple of medical humor.
videos.w: Commenters call it a classic worth rewatching over and over.

videos.t: Surgical Knot Tying: One-handed, Righty
videos.s: A tutorial demonstrating one-handed surgical knot tying.
videos.w: Students suggest learning it before the surgery rotation to impress attendings.

videos.t: Fred Rogers: Look for the Helpers
videos.s: Clip of Fred Rogers on looking for the helpers in times of trauma.
videos.w: Commenters say the idea helped them cope with distressing calls and thank healthcare workers for being helpers.

videos.t: Nursing School | Study Smarter, Not Harder
videos.s: Nurse Nacole gives short study-strategy advice for nursing school.
videos.w: Students say her videos helped them and recommend them to others starting out.

videos.t: My Memorization Technique in Med School | A Typical Weekend in Med School VLOG | ANKI tutorial
videos.s: A med student vlog on memorization methods, showing a weekend of studying and how to use Anki with image occlusion.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as an example of using image occlusion for charts and pathways and of active recall.

videos.t: Anti-Depressants Are So Not A Big Deal - feat. Michael Hyatt - "Crazy Ex-Girlfriend"
videos.s: A comedy song from the TV show Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, performed by Michael Hyatt, about how antidepressants are not a big deal.
videos.w: People newly on an SSRI, or worried about starting one, say it makes them feel better about taking antidepressants.

videos.t: Bondi Lifeguards Resuscitate Korean Tourist Ryan Kim (Dead for 5 minutes!)
videos.s: Bondi Rescue episode in which lifeguards resuscitate a drowned tourist, with an explanation of the drowning resuscitation sequence.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for better-quality CPR and for explaining the DRS at the start.

videos.t: How I became a doctor in Switzerland (UK experience)
videos.s: Personal video by a UK-trained doctor about how she became a doctor in Switzerland and what training there is like.
videos.w: Pointed out to UK doctors curious about working in Swiss training.

videos.t: MY FIRST SKILLS CHECK-OFF
videos.s: A Nurse Blake comedy sketch about a nursing student's first skills check-off.
videos.w: Commenters call it funny, worth a laugh no matter how many times you have seen it.

videos.t: IBR vs PAYE vs REPAYE for Medical Students
videos.s: An analysis comparing federal income-driven student loan repayment plans (IBR, PAYE, REPAYE) for medical students and residents.
videos.w: Commenters say it clarifies the differences between the plans and used it to brush up before choosing.

videos.t: Chasing Zero: Winning the War on Healthcare Harm
videos.s: A documentary on patient safety and preventable harm in health care.
videos.w: Viewers call it eye-opening and moving, a reminder to slow down and double-check to prevent errors.

videos.t: A Real Doctor (& Tom) Watch A Vaccine "Debate" | ZDoggMD.com
videos.s: ZDoggMD and a colleague watch and react to a vaccine debate.
videos.w: A commenter calls it the level-headed vaccine debate video that is needed.

videos.t: The Coronavirus Explained & What You Should Do
videos.s: Kurzgesagt animated explainer on the coronavirus and what individuals should do, made with expert consultation and sources.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains the basics, debunks myths and shows why social distancing slows spread.

videos.t: Side Effects of SSRIs Presented in an Understandable Way (Details and Management of Each Symptom)
videos.s: A Psychofarm video going through the side effects of SSRIs one by one, with ways to manage each.
videos.w: A commenter calls it an excellent symptom-by-symptom review with management strategies.

videos.t: Don't Be the Last Person to Die
videos.s: CGP Grey short animated essay arguing that aging and death are a problem worth defeating. It is paired with a follow-up from Kurzgesagt.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a concise, fun statement of the case that curing aging matters most.

videos.t: Vitamin D and COVID 19: The Evidence for Prevention and Treatment of Coronavirus (SARS CoV 2)
videos.s: MedCram lecture reviewing the evidence on vitamin D for preventing and treating COVID-19.
videos.w: Recommended as a well put together video from a channel commenters enjoy for nerding out on medicine.

videos.t: Electron transport chain
videos.s: Short Harvard Online animated lesson on the mitochondrial electron transport chain. It shows proton pumping and the machinery that drives ATP synthesis.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for the nanomachine feel of cell biology, with molecular machines holding a proton gradient across the membrane.

videos.t: What Does Serotonin Do? (The 2 Serotonin Receptor Types and Why serotonin is Important)
videos.s: A Psychofarm video on the roles of serotonin and its 5HT1A and 5HT2A receptors and how SSRIs act on them.
videos.w: A commenter calls it an incredible video that gives insight into serotonin receptors and SSRIs.

videos.t: Doctor Says Striking NHS Consultants “Just Want Their Pay To Be Restored To Pre-Pandemic Levels”
videos.s: TV interview in which an NHS consultant argues that striking consultants only want pay restored to pre-pandemic levels.
videos.w: Commenters praise the doctor's composed performance against a hostile interviewer.

videos.t: Bed Bugs- What You've Been Told is Totally False
videos.s: Mark Rober video on bed bugs and what common beliefs about them get wrong.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for evidence-based ways to defend against bed bugs and as reassurance that infestations are less bad than feared.

videos.t: PEEP Part 1
videos.s: Ten-minute explanation of PEEP from TheAncientScholar.
videos.w: A commenter says it explained PEEP more clearly than three hours of professor teaching.

videos.t: Pharmacy Myths #1
videos.s: The first video in a Pharmacy Myths series by Gina Tandarich on common public misunderstandings about pharmacists and pharmacies.
videos.w: A commenter says pharmacists who have been yelled at over a misunderstanding should share it.

videos.t: Mary Ellen Farr Interview - The challenges of being a nurse - Cherokee Workwear 10th anniversary
videos.s: An interview with experienced nurse Mary Ellen Farr about the challenges of being a nurse, made for a uniform brand's 10th anniversary.
videos.w: A commenter calls it the best nursing survival guide they have seen.

videos.t: Patients at Risk #2: Nurse Practitioner Speaks Out Against Independent Practice
videos.s: Episode 2 of the Patients at Risk series, in which a nurse practitioner speaks out against independent practice for midlevel providers.
videos.w: A commenter praises the NP for saying that the midlevel push is a money grab and that diploma mills are a scam.

videos.t: Atropelamento, em apoio ao CBM
videos.s: Uncut Brazilian paramedic call footage of a pedestrian struck by a vehicle, from a channel supporting the fire brigade.
videos.w: A commenter calls the channel some of the best documentation of the paramedic profession they have seen.

videos.t: Mel Herbert Keynote Address, ACEP 2018
videos.s: Mel Herberts keynote address at the ACEP 2018 emergency medicine conference.
videos.w: Commenters call it a powerful, inspiring speech that can lift you out of burnout.

videos.t: Tim Minchin: Storm
videos.s: A live performance of Tim Minchins nine-minute beat poem Storm, a satirical piece against alternative medicine.
videos.w: Commenters call it a funny, cathartic piece on alternative medicine worth the ten minutes.

videos.t: SSRIs in the Brain: Understand Anti-Depressants and Why Anti-Depressants Take So Long to Work
videos.s: A Psychofarm video on how SSRIs act in the brain and why antidepressants take weeks to work.
videos.w: A commenter calls it an excellent explanation of how SSRIs work and why they take 4-6 weeks.

videos.t: New Technique for Umbilical Artery Catheter Placement in the Neonate
videos.s: A demonstration of a technique for placing an umbilical artery catheter in a neonate that avoids false tracks.
videos.w: A commenter says it should be the standard method of teaching placement.

videos.t: Harvey Cushing and the Discovery of the Pituitary Gland - Let's Talk About Hormones | Corporis
videos.s: An episode of the Corporis series on hormones, telling the story of Harvey Cushing and the discovery of the pituitary gland.
videos.w: A commenter calls the channel's hormone series excellent despite barely any views.

videos.t: Greed and the Pharmaceutical Industry-Ron Piana
videos.s: A 45-minute interview with medical writer Ron Piana, who is critical of the pharmaceutical industry, including its marketing of Avastin.
videos.w: A pharmacy commenter found the interview interesting and worth the 45 minutes.

videos.t: ThedaCare TRO DISMISSED, Ascension & Employees WIN!! (ThedaCare v. Ascension)
videos.s: A law-channel breakdown of the court ruling in the ThedaCare versus Ascension dispute over health system staff and a restraining order.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a clear overview of the decision and the reasons behind it.

videos.t: Paleo Diet & Strength Training Biochemistry | Doug McGuff M.D. | Full Length HD
videos.s: Doug McGuff presents the biochemistry behind high-intensity strength training and the paleo diet, including how the body stores and burns fat. It is a roughly hour-and-a-half full-length lecture.
videos.w: Commenters list it among resources on high-intensity training and note its last part covers medical-school biochemistry and metabolism.

videos.t: The Problem With Weed…
videos.s: HealthyGamerGG, hosted by a psychiatrist known as Dr K, discusses cannabis use and dependence, with advice on meditation.
videos.w: One commenter calls it the best explanation of weed addiction they have seen.

videos.t: The mathematics of weight loss | Ruben Meerman | TEDxQUT (edited version)
videos.s: TEDx talk in which Ruben Meerman shows with lab demonstrations where fat goes when it is lost. He argues that most of it is exhaled as carbon dioxide.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a clear, 20-minute account of the physics and arithmetic of weight loss that counters diet myths.

videos.t: SSRI Differences (Sertraline Escitalopram Citalopram Fluoxetine Fluvoxamine Paroxetine)
videos.s: A Psychofarm video comparing the six main SSRIs: sertraline, escitalopram, citalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine and paroxetine.
videos.w: A commenter calls it an excellent way to learn how the six main SSRIs differ.

videos.t: COVID-19 How to Use One Ventilator to Save Multiple Lives
videos.s: A video showing how one ventilator can be split to support several patients, made during the COVID-19 surge by one of the people proposing the approach.
videos.w: Commenters say it is worth watching as a demonstration of ventilator sharing.

videos.t: The Middlemen of Healthcare
videos.s: A short comedy skit by Dr. Glaucomflecken about pharmacy benefit managers and what they do in the US healthcare system.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a funny two-minute explanation of PBMs that sums up what is wrong with healthcare.

videos.t: ICN Victoria - Hosegood on In-Flight Medical Emergencies Part 1
videos.s: A dinner talk by airline medical director Ian Hosegood on in-flight medical emergencies and how diversion decisions are made.
videos.w: A commenter found his account of crew priorities and the cost of diversion fascinating.

videos.t: Whole-brain imaging of neuronal activity in a larval zebrafish
videos.s: A Discover Magazine video of whole-brain imaging of neural activity in a larval zebrafish at single-cell resolution.
videos.w: A commenter calls it the best video for getting a sense of what brain activity looks like.

videos.t: The food revolution - AHS 2011
videos.s: A Diet Doctor lecture from the 2011 Ancestral Health Symposium making the case for dietary change, particularly in carbohydrates.
videos.w: A clinician says it changed how they treat diabetic patients and sums up what they try to get across.

videos.t: The Physician in Modern Society
videos.s: A Stanford lecture by Abraham Verghese on the physician in modern society, including earning patients' trust through the exam and listening.
videos.w: Commenters say every medical student should watch it.

videos.t: NIH Obesity Research Task Force Symposium: Medications to Treat Obesity: Past, Present, and Future
videos.ch: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
videos.s: An NIH symposium talk by Randy Seeley reviewing medications for obesity, from past drugs to incretin-based therapies and what comes next.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it to skeptics and anyone wanting to get up to speed on the research behind obesity drugs.

videos.t: Shawn Christopher Shea, MD  Video 1 Psychiatric Interviewing
videos.s: The first video in a series with Shawn Christopher Shea, author of Psychiatric Interviewing, on interview technique including suicide risk assessment.
videos.w: Commenters say the piecemeal series is handy for clerkship teaching and call the three-part suicide risk set brilliant.

videos.t: The Emergency Room: A Window into Us | Louis Profeta | TEDxWabashCollege
videos.s: A TEDx talk by emergency physician Louis Profeta on what the emergency room reveals about us.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives insight into the mind of an EM physician and accurately portrays working in emergency medicine.

videos.t: Ear Pain 5: Otoscope Examination
videos.s: Part 5 of an ear pain series by MjSylvesterMD showing how to perform an otoscope examination.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for how to hold an otoscope and as good exam instruction.

videos.t: The Gym of Life
videos.s: Not Just Bikes argues that people in walkable, bikeable Dutch cities stay healthy because exercise is built into daily life, which he calls the gym of life. It contrasts this with car-dependent cities that need deliberate workouts.
videos.w: Commenters note that it shows disliking cycling is often about the city rather than cycling, and that it makes the case for city design as a health investment.

videos.t: Dr. Satchin Panda on Time-Restricted Feeding and Its Effects on Obesity, Muscle Mass & Heart Health
videos.s: Rhonda Patrick interviews Salk Institute researcher Satchidananda Panda about circadian rhythms and meal timing. They cover time-restricted feeding and its links to obesity, muscle mass, heart health and light exposure.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for Panda's circadian-focused eating research and for details on fasting and coffee.

videos.t: Dr. Jason Fung - 'The Aetiology of Obesity'
videos.s: Nephrologist Jason Fung presents his view of the causes of obesity and type 2 diabetes, focusing on hormones such as insulin rather than calories alone, and draws on research and his Intensive Dietary Management program.
videos.w: Commenters call it a research-heavy talk by a doctor and a decent introduction to how hormones regulate fat stores.

videos.t: USMLE Step 1 - Biostatistics - (EXTRA)
videos.s: Randy Neil's USMLE Step 1 biostatistics video, part of a playlist covering the statistics needed for the exam.
videos.w: Commenters say the playlist covers the biostatistics needed for USMLE and suggest following it with UWorld questions.

videos.t: The Matching Algorithm - Explained
videos.s: An explanation of how the residency Matching Algorithm works, from National Matching Services.
videos.w: Viewers call it one of the better explanations of the Match and say it shows why to rank programs by your own preference.

videos.t: How to Use Anki for Med School
videos.s: The AnKing introduction to using Anki for medical school, including suspending and unsuspending cards by topic.
videos.w: Commenters tell newcomers to watch it to learn how Anki works before downloading decks.

videos.t: Anki: The V2 Experimental Scheduler
videos.s: The AnKing video on the Anki V2 experimental scheduler and custom filtered decks.
videos.w: Users say it explains the scheduler requirement, and one reports it plus updating fixed their AnKing deck problem.

videos.t: Med School Musical - A Disney Parody - University of Alberta
videos.s: The University of Alberta Med School Musical, a nine-minute Disney parody about medical school.
videos.w: Commenters call it well written and produced, with great singers and songs.

videos.t: Study Tips - How to learn new content
videos.s: Ali Abdaal video of study tips on how to learn new content using active recall and understanding.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains understanding well and encourages active learning over passive watching.

videos.t: How To Calm A Crying Baby - Dr. Robert Hamilton Demonstrates "The Hold" (Official)
videos.s: Pediatrician Dr. Robert Hamilton demonstrates The Hold, a technique for calming a crying baby.
videos.w: Commenters call it a cool trick that worked like a charm until about six months of age.

videos.t: Guided Meditation for Detachment From Over-Thinking (Anxiety / OCD / Depression)
videos.s: A guided meditation aimed at detaching from over-thinking, framed for anxiety, OCD and depression.
videos.w: Students and nurses say they listen to it in bed to calm rumination and fall asleep.

videos.t: The Milk-Industrial Complex: Why You Don't Need to Drink Milk
videos.s: Short Healthcare Triage episode by Aaron Carroll arguing that milk gets an undeserved pass in efforts to improve diets. It examines claims about calcium and bone strength and concludes people do not need to drink milk.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a great video on milk, with detail on calcium, sugar and anemia, from a co-author of the article under discussion.

videos.t: Strokes & The Rule of 4s || USMLE
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine USMLE video on strokes and the rule of 4s for localizing brainstem lesions.
videos.w: Students say it helped them with brainstem localization and that you need it for brainstem lesions.

videos.t: How I Scored 272 Without Taking a SINGLE Note (USMLE)
videos.s: Video by a student who scored 272 on Step 1 explaining why he did it without taking notes and mainly by doing questions.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as an argument against annotating and for active learning.

videos.t: Anki: How To Do Anki Faster (and stay focused!)
videos.s: The AnKing video on doing Anki faster and staying focused, introducing the speed focus add-on.
videos.w: Users say the add-on solves speed and focus problems and link it as exactly what they were after.

videos.t: Anki: Install 40+ Add-ons in 5 minutes
videos.s: The AnKing short video on installing more than 40 Anki add-ons in about five minutes.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for getting started with add-ons and searching a premade deck.

videos.t: High Yield Internal Medicine - Emma Holiday
videos.s: A high-yield internal medicine review lecture by Emma Holliday, reposted on another channel.
videos.w: Students use it as a crash-course review that earned a few NBME points.

videos.t: Peritoneum Anatomy: From Basics to Clinical Application
videos.s: A lecture on peritoneum anatomy from basics to clinical application by The Noted Anatomist.
videos.w: Students say it made a confusing topic click.

videos.t: Emma Holliday Internal Medicine W/ Her Slides| USMLE Step 1 2 Shelf Board Exam | PowerPoint Download
videos.s: Emma Holliday's internal medicine review lecture with slides, aimed at USMLE and shelf exams.
videos.w: Commenters say it covers most high-yield medicine shelf topics and matched the actual test.

videos.t: Deskbound | Kelly Starrett | Talks at Google
videos.s: Kelly Starrett's Talks at Google presentation on staying healthy while desk-bound, mixing anatomy with practical mobility advice. It shows how to set up a desk and how to sit and move to avoid pain.
videos.w: Commenters give it as the first step for fixing posture, with guidance on how to sit, mobility and stretching.

videos.t: The surprising science of happiness | Dan Gilbert
videos.s: A TED talk by psychologist Dan Gilbert on the science of happiness, including impact bias and how we mispredict what will make us happy.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a TED talk on choosing to be happy that explains impact bias well, with interesting statistics.

videos.t: Is a Calorie a Calorie?  Processed Food, Experiment Gone Wrong
videos.s: Stanford Health Care event with Christopher Gardner and Robert Lustig on whether all calories are equal, focusing on processed food and sugar. It questions whether calories in versus calories out explains weight and health.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for Lustig's case that processed food and calories are not equivalent.

videos.t: Salmonella's Salmon Diner - SketchyMicro / Sketchy Medical (USMLE Step 1)
videos.s: A Sketchy Medical SketchyMicro episode on Salmonella, using an illustrated story to teach microbiology for USMLE Step 1.
videos.w: Students call SketchyMicro the best visual learning tool for microbiology and say it can inspire illustrated notes.

videos.t: Matt Might - Winning the War on Error Solving the Halting Problem and Curing Cancer
videos.s: Matt Might's Curry On talk on ending errors in code, both software and the human genome. He covers static analysis as a way to approximate the halting problem and a computational approach to precision medicine.
videos.w: Commenters call it an amazing, must-see talk that introduces static analysis alongside the speaker's personal story.

videos.t: How to Update Anki Decks with the special fields add-on to preserve scheduling & edits (Pre-AnkiHub)
videos.s: The AnKing guide to updating Anki decks with the Special Fields add-on to preserve scheduling and edits, from before AnkiHub.
videos.w: Users say it gives step-by-step instructions for keeping progress and importing only errata updates.

videos.t: How to Approach Missed Questions and Make Anki Flashcards
videos.s: The AnKing explains how to analyze missed practice questions and turn them into effective Anki flashcards.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for how to examine missed questions and make good cards from them.

videos.t: Why Age? Should We End Aging Forever?
videos.s: Kurzgesagt short animated video asking whether humanity should try to end aging, and arguing the case for curing age-related disease. It is part one of a pair, with a second part by CGP Grey.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a compelling argument that curing aging matters most and a good answer to common objections.

videos.t: The effects of DBS on the motor symptoms of Parkinson's Disease
videos.s: Short patient video from a man diagnosed with early onset Parkinson's at 35, showing how deep brain stimulation surgery has controlled his motor symptoms. It shows his tremors with the stimulator off and on.
videos.w: Commenters say the on/off comparison shows how impressive deep brain stimulation technology is.

videos.t: Determining Causality: A Review of the Bradford Hill Criteria
videos.s: A review of the Bradford Hill criteria for determining causation in epidemiology.
videos.w: Step 1 studiers say it covers the Bradford Hill criteria well enough for the exam.

videos.t: How I overcame alcoholism | Claudia Christian | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool
videos.s: Actress Claudia Christian tells how she overcame alcoholism with the Sinclair Method, which uses naltrexone to gradually reduce cravings, and discusses new perspectives on treating alcohol use disorder.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as the talk that convinced them to try the Sinclair Method and as a resource on it.

videos.t: Build a Do-It-Yourself Air Purifier for About $40
videos.s: Michigan Medicine demonstration of building a cheap DIY air purifier from a box fan and a HEPA or high-MERV filter using hardware-store parts. It explains why this helps against dust, smoke and viruses and ties it to local air quality readings.
videos.w: Commenters say the cheap purifier relieved their allergy symptoms within days and that a furnace filter on a fan is good enough.

videos.t: Medical Embryology - Difficult Concepts of Early Development Explained Simply
videos.s: A Clinical Anatomy Explained lecture on the difficult concepts of early embryonic development, taught simply.
videos.w: Students say it gives a good general foundation in key embryology concepts and that the educator has many related videos.

videos.t: Brachial Plexus Made Insanely Easy
videos.s: Shan Nanji video teaching the brachial plexus with a memory method.
videos.w: Students say the method stuck for months and teaches the plexus well.

videos.t: Genetic Engineering Will Change Everything Forever – CRISPR
videos.s: Kurzgesagt animated explainer on CRISPR gene editing, covering how the technology works and what it could mean for curing disease, designer babies and aging.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a quick, basic introduction to gene editing.

videos.t: How to Study for USMLE Step 1
videos.s: Video giving a study plan and technique for USMLE Step 1.
videos.w: Commenters say it makes Step 1 studying seem manageable and call it some of the best advice out there.

videos.t: Sensitivity, Specificity, PPV, NPV
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video explaining sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it alongside the Randy Neil videos as gold for biostatistics.

videos.t: Isha Kriya: A Guided Meditation For Health And Wellbeing | 15-Minutes
videos.s: A 15-minute guided meditation, the Isha Kriya, from Sadhguru, with an explanation of the practice.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as well explained and calming, including before bed.

videos.t: USMLE Step 1 High Yield Images (Part 1)
videos.s: The first part of Med School Moose's USMLE Step 1 high-yield images series, reviewing images commonly tested on the exam.
videos.w: Commenters pair the playlist with the NBME images PDF and Anki and note it can be watched at 2x.

videos.t: How To Answer USMLE Step 1 Questions Like A Pro
videos.s: TheMDJourney on how to approach USMLE Step 1 questions, including how to read and narrow answer choices.
videos.w: A commenter says it changed their mentality on avoiding second-guessing and misreading questions.

videos.t: Drugs of Abuse (Mechanism, Intoxication, Withdrawal, & Associations)
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video on drugs of abuse, covering mechanisms, intoxication, withdrawal and associations.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a good way to study intoxication and withdrawal syndromes for Step 2.

videos.t: How dangerous are magnetic items near an MRI magnet?
videos.s: A practiCal fMRI video demonstrating how dangerous magnetic objects become near an MRI magnet, with the physics behind the hazard.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows the safety risks of metal in the scanner room and is good medical physics.

videos.t: How to Study for Exams - Spaced Repetition | Evidence-based revision tips
videos.s: Ali Abdaal explains spaced repetition and other evidence-based revision techniques for exams.
videos.w: Commenters call it a must-watch for exam studying and for learning active study techniques.

videos.t: Stroke Chart- USMLE Step 1 High Yield
videos.s: A seven-minute stroke chart review for USMLE Step 1 that walks through a diagram of stroke syndromes.
videos.w: Students say they draw the diagram from it and answer all the stroke questions correctly.

videos.t: USMLE STEP 1: COMMUNICATION VIDEO #2 - EMPATHY + READINESS FOR CHANGE
videos.s: A Randy Neil USMLE Step 1 communication video, number 2, on empathy and readiness for change.
videos.w: Students say watching his communication videos paid off on the exam.

videos.t: High Yield Pediatrics Review for Step 2 CK & Shelf Exam (Part 1 of 2)
videos.s: Doctor High Yield's pediatrics review for the Step 2 CK and shelf exam, part 1 of 2.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best last-minute pediatrics review and say it helped them answer exam questions.

videos.t: Coagulation Cascade | Part 1/12
videos.s: Part 1 of 12 in Dr. Najeeb's lecture series on the coagulation cascade.
videos.w: Students say it explains the cascade step by step, though it takes a lot of time.

videos.t: Physiology of Lipoprotein Metabolism
videos.s: A lecture on the physiology of lipoprotein metabolism, covering apolipoproteins and lipoprotein types.
videos.w: Students say it makes the lipoprotein pathways easier to understand and is good for learning apolipoproteins.

videos.t: Thoughts On Suicide
videos.s: A short motivational clip by Elliott Hulse on thoughts about suicide.
videos.w: A commenter urges a distressed student to watch it as a short motivational clip for someone feeling stuck.

videos.t: Brain stem lesions chart for Neuro review Step 1
videos.s: Chart-based review of brain stem lesions for Step 1 neurology.
videos.w: Students say it earns a few questions per exam and call it golden.

videos.t: How to Get Over a Breakup
videos.s: A self-help video on how to get over a breakup.
videos.w: A medical student says it helped after a breakup and still watches it for that.

videos.t: Did SARS-Cov-2 start in a Chinese lab?
videos.s: Science journalist potholer54 examines the claim that SARS-CoV-2 came from a Wuhan lab, tracing the sources behind it and the weaknesses in the evidence.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a methodical takedown of lab-leak claims.

videos.t: Valter Longo, Ph.D. on Fasting-Mimicking Diet & Fasting for Longevity, Cancer & Multiple Sclerosis
videos.s: Rhonda Patrick interviews USC gerontologist Valter Longo about fasting, the fasting-mimicking diet and their effects on longevity, cancer and multiple sclerosis. They discuss mechanisms such as IGF-1 and autophagy and clinical trials.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a deeper dive on water fasting, the fasting-mimicking diet and the clinical trials behind them.

videos.t: Dr. Bill Harris on the Omega-3 Index: Increasing Omega-3 to Promote Longevity & Transform Health
videos.s: Rhonda Patrick interviews Dr. Bill Harris, co-inventor of the Omega-3 Index and author of more than 300 papers on fatty acids. They cover EPA and DHA dosing, fish oil trials such as REDUCE-IT, and how omega-3 levels relate to health and longevity.
videos.w: Commenters take from it that most people underdose omega-3, and that omega-3 levels are linked to mortality risk and inflammation.

videos.t: Geoffrey West on COMPLEXITY
videos.s: Physicist Geoffrey West speaks at an FQXi conference about complexity and scaling laws. He covers how metabolism, growth and lifespan scale across organisms and how the same mathematics applies to cities and companies.
videos.w: Commenters call it a comprehensive, accessible 40-minute introduction to scaling in organisms and cities.

videos.t: Homeless man talks openly about being addicted to heroin. We have an opioid crisis in America.
videos.s: Short street interview from Invisible People with Keith, a homeless man in Los Angeles who lost his housing-industry job in the crash and moved from painkillers to heroin because it was cheaper. He talks candidly about the grip of addiction.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a powerful, honest firsthand account of heroin addiction.

videos.t: Depression is a disease of civilization: Stephen Ilardi at TEDxEmory
videos.s: TEDx talk in which clinical psychologist Stephen Ilardi argues that depression is a disease of modern civilization and presents a lifestyle-based program to treat it without drugs. Topics include exercise, sunlight, omega-3s and social connection.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for understanding and coping with depression through lifestyle, and for the argument that hunter-gatherer genes mismatch sedentary modern life.

videos.t: How to Cure Aging – During Your Lifetime?
videos.s: Kurzgesagt animated explainer on whether aging could be cured within our lifetimes, made with Lifespan.io and the LEAF foundation. It introduces the idea of treating aging as a medical problem.
videos.w: Commenters call it a great introduction to aging research, and one says it changed their view on ending aging.

videos.t: 2012 Burnett Lecture Part 1 Keynote Speaker: Russell A. Barkley, Ph.D.
videos.s: Russell Barkley's keynote at UNC's 2012 Burnett Seminar on ADHD. He presents it as an executive function disorder and discusses its effects and how to help.
videos.w: Commenters urge people to watch it to learn about ADHD, including its cognitive psychology beyond brain scans and how accountability prompts help.

videos.t: Doctor Dissects the Wim Hof Method - Cold Hard Science Analysis
videos.s: Cardiologist Rohin Francis of Medlife Crisis runs a detailed, skeptical review of the Wim Hof Method, covering research on cold exposure and breathing techniques. It also teaches how to read scientific statistics critically.
videos.w: Commenters call it an amazing summary of the research from a skeptical doctor.

videos.t: Myopia: A Modern Yet Reversible Disease — Todd Becker, M.S. (AHS14)
videos.s: Todd Becker's Ancestral Health Symposium talk arguing that myopia is driven by near-work and can be reversed. It covers the biology and epidemiology and experimental evidence for reversal using weaker lenses.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a non-surgical method that reduced one person's prescription, and one calls it life-changing.

videos.t: Your Brain: Who's in Control? | Full Documentary | NOVA | PBS
videos.s: NOVA documentary with neuroscientist Heather Berlin exploring the subconscious and what drives our decisions. It uses sleepwalking, anesthesia, improvised rap in an MRI and game theory to probe how much of the brain's work is hidden.
videos.w: Commenters call it a great resource on how much of experienced reality is filled in by the brain.

videos.t: Why Adults Can't Develop Perfect Pitch
videos.s: Rick Beato argues that adults cannot develop true perfect pitch, tying it to critical-period brain plasticity and language acquisition. He discusses the research behind this.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best video on perfect pitch, and one says it convinced them adults cannot train it.

videos.t: Breakthrough with Healing Chronic Pain | Howard Schubiner | Talks at Google
videos.s: Talks at Google presentation by Dr. Howard Schubiner on his research that much chronic pain comes from learned neural pathways rather than structural damage. He outlines a treatment approach based on that view.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a rigorous yet balanced talk on pain that does not mean injury.

videos.t: Michael Levin: Consciousness, Biology, Universal Mind, Emergence, Cancer Research
videos.s: Curt Jaimungal interviews Tufts biologist Michael Levin about consciousness, bioelectricity, emergence and cancer research. The conversation challenges reductionist views of life.
videos.w: Commenters call it a mind-blowing conversation with examples like bioelectric signals that build frog embryo eyes.

videos.t: Salt: Are you getting Enough?   (More Sodium & Health)
videos.s: Joseph Everett argues, drawing on the book The Salt Fix, that most people benefit from more rather than less salt. He reviews studies on sodium, potassium and blood pressure.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for studies suggesting high salt intake does better when paired with high potassium, and for the point that salt intake has halved over a century.

videos.t: The Deadliest Being on Planet Earth – The Bacteriophage
videos.s: Animated Kurzgesagt explainer on bacteriophages, the viruses that kill bacteria. It covers how they infect and burst cells and their potential as therapy against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
videos.w: Commenters call it an accessible animated explanation of everything about bacteriophages and their promise against superbugs.

videos.t: Vertigo Myth:  BPPV = Dix-Hallpike test, the patient gets dizzy, and you see nystagmus
videos.s: A short teaching video on why diagnosing BPPV takes more than a Dix-Hallpike test that makes the patient dizzy with nystagmus.
videos.w: Posted as a correction to the common idea that dizziness and nystagmus on Dix-Hallpike are enough to diagnose BPPV.

videos.t: EXPECTATION vs REALITY in RADIOLOGY - How to read a Complicated Chest X-Ray
videos.s: Dr. Cellini explains how to read a complicated chest X-ray, contrasting expectation with reality in radiology.
videos.w: A commenter recommends it as another very good chest X-ray teaching video.

videos.t: How to screen for central features and use HINTS plus to diagnose vestibular neuritis
videos.s: A teaching video on screening for central causes and using HINTS plus to diagnose vestibular neuritis in acute vertigo.
videos.w: A commenter shares it as a guide to when patients with acute vertigo and nystagmus can be sent home.

videos.t: Doctor Reacts to Middle Ground: Pro-Vaccine vs Anti-Vaccine
videos.s: Doctor Mike reacts to a Middle Ground debate between pro-vaccine and anti-vaccine participants.
videos.w: Commenters say he handles the vaccine debate more empathetically and takes apart arguments without personal attacks.

videos.t: Roundtable on Lowering Healthcare Costs and Bringing Transparency to Prescription Drug Middlemen
videos.s: A White House roundtable on lowering healthcare costs and on the role of pharmacy benefit managers, the prescription drug middlemen. The discussion centers on how PBM practices affect community pharmacies.
videos.w: A commenter says everyone in healthcare should watch this discussion of PBM abuses.

videos.t: First 4 Minutes of NBC’s New Workplace Comedy | St. Denis Medical | Sneak Peek
videos.s: The first four minutes of St. Denis Medical, an NBC workplace comedy set in a hospital, released as a sneak peek.
videos.w: A nurse recommends the new medical comedy series.

videos.t: COVID 2019 China Infection Control Measures Described
videos.s: A video describing infection control measures used in China during the early COVID-19 outbreak, including PPE donning and doffing and sealed shifts.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a detailed protocol, with accurate instructions for taking off PPE.

videos.t: Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) vs. Medical Doctor (MD)
videos.s: A 2010 comedy sketch satirizing the debate between Doctor of Nursing Practice and MD training.
videos.w: A commenter reposts it as a prophetic gem that foresaw the scope-of-practice debate.

videos.t: Differences between Anti-Psychotics: Quetiapine, Olanzapine, Clozapine
videos.s: A Psychofarm video comparing three antipsychotics: quetiapine, olanzapine and clozapine.
videos.w: A commenter recommends it as a great review of how the three drugs differ.

videos.t: Inducing syncope: the fainting lark
videos.s: Syncopedia footage of young people deliberately induced to faint, showing the convulsive movements that can look like a seizure.
videos.w: Commenters use it to teach how syncope differs from seizure and call it a favorite video.

videos.t: The Proximal Humerus: Ch. 3 - Subclavian Vein Focus with the Arrow® EZ-IO® System
videos.s: A Teleflex product video on intraosseous access at the proximal humerus with the Arrow EZ-IO system, focusing on the subclavian vein.
videos.w: A commenter recommends it as a view of how well humeral IO access works.

videos.t: A Review of Anti-Psychotic Onset of Action (How Long Do Anti-Psychotics Take? Anti-Psychotic Drug)
videos.s: A Psychofarm video reviewing how long antipsychotics take to start working.
videos.w: A commenter recommends it as a nifty review of antipsychotic onset of action.

videos.t: Debating The Value Of Eastern Medicine (Ayurveda) | Healthy Gamer Dr. K
videos.s: A long podcast conversation between Doctor Mike and Dr. K about Ayurveda and Eastern medicine, weighing population-level research against individual practice.
videos.w: Commenters call it a long but great discussion.

videos.t: How Bullying Is Different for Women
videos.s: HealthyGamerGG video on how bullying differs for women, with tips for handling workplace bullying.
videos.w: Commenters found it illuminating on female bullying and useful for coping with it.

videos.t: Understand SNRIs Better: Duloxetine and Venlafaxine
videos.s: A Psychofarm video on SNRIs, focusing on duloxetine and venlafaxine and how they act.
videos.w: A commenter says it helps with understanding SNRIs and dosing Effexor and Cymbalta.

videos.t: What happened to Irvo Otieno? Full security video shows final moments.
videos.s: News video of security footage from the Irvo Otieno case, including the EMS response.
videos.w: A commenter found the calm, organized EMS response refreshing compared with videos of incompetence.

videos.t: THIRD NERVE PALSY - PUPIL SPARING
videos.s: A clinical example video showing a pupil-sparing third nerve palsy.
videos.w: A commenter says it is a good example of a pupil-sparing third nerve palsy.

videos.t: Bill Burr on Coronavirus Quarantine, Rants About Mask Wearing
videos.s: A Bill Burr stand-up clip about coronavirus quarantine and mask wearing, responding to an anti-mask rant.
videos.w: A commenter shares it as Bill Burr shutting down Joe Rogans anti-mask rant.

videos.t: Cephalosporins - Antibiotics Explained Clearly
videos.s: A MedCram lecture on cephalosporins, explaining the antibiotic class.
videos.w: A commenter recommends it as a clear explanation of cephalosporins.

videos.t: The £500,000 question in Healthcare - the legal challenge over Physician Associates
videos.s: Short explainer from Anaesthetists United on their legal challenge over physician associates and anaesthesia associates.
videos.w: A commenter says it explains why the action matters for patient care and asks others to share it.

videos.t: What Medical School DOESN'T Teach You
videos.s: A Med School Insiders video on what medical school does not teach, with advice to premeds about physician-led care.
videos.w: A commenter found it uplifting for its advice to premeds to join a physician-advocacy group and back physician-led care.

videos.t: How Nursing Homes Hide Profits While Residents Suffer
videos.s: A VICE News report on how nursing home operators generate profit while residents receive poor care.
videos.w: A commenter shares it as an interesting and infuriating look at nursing homes claiming to be poor while profiting.

videos.t: A World of Hurt: How Medical Malpractice Fails Everyone
videos.s: A documentary from Ocean State Media on how the medical malpractice system works and fails patients and doctors.
videos.w: A commenter says the documentary on malpractice litigation shook them.

videos.t: Her DEATH TOUCH baffled doctors
videos.s: MrBallen retells the case of Gloria Ramirez, the patient whose 1994 emergency room visit made staff ill.
videos.w: A commenter calls it a gripping retelling of the incident.

videos.t: I Don't Know - Med School Parody of "Let It Go" from Frozen (University of Chicago Pritzker SOM)
videos.s: I Dont Know, a University of Chicago Pritzker School of Medicine parody of Let It Go from Frozen about third-year medical students.
videos.w: Commenters, including a nursing student, say it is funny and got a hearty laugh.

videos.t: Coronavirus Pandemic Update 37: The ACE-2 Receptor - The Doorway to COVID-19 (ACE Inhibitors & ARBs)
videos.s: A MedCram coronavirus update on the ACE-2 receptor as the entry point for COVID-19 and what it means for ACE inhibitor and ARB use.
videos.w: A commenter calls it a good, detailed summary of recommendations on ACE and ARB use in COVID.

videos.t: So You Want to Be a NURSE PRACTITIONER [Ep. 25]
videos.s: A Med School Insiders episode on becoming a nurse practitioner, covering training, scope creep and team roles.
videos.w: Commenters share it for its take on NP risks and for what it takes to become one.

videos.t: Weed for Addiction, PTSD, Sleep, and More?! | Weed QnA with Dr. Hsu
videos.s: HealthyGamerGG Q&A with Dr. Hsu on cannabis, covering its use for addiction, PTSD and sleep and how potency has changed.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it to hear two experts discuss cannabis and find it informative on the rise in potency.

videos.t: An Off-Label Guide to Gabapentin | Anxiety, Sleep, Addiction, Pain, & More
videos.s: A Carlat Psychiatry Report video guiding clinicians through off-label uses of gabapentin for anxiety, sleep, addiction and pain.
videos.w: A commenter notes it is the first of a series of free, high-quality weekly psychiatry videos from Carlat.

videos.t: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Bryan Johnson, founder of Kernel, about brain-computer interfaces and Kernel non-invasive brain monitoring hardware. It covers what the devices can do today and the company plans.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good starting point for what the Kernel Flow helmet and its infrared sensing can do.

videos.t: Open drop ether: No. 2 (1944) Pt. 2 of 2
videos.s: Archival Wellcome Library film from 1944 showing open drop ether anesthesia, part 2 of 2.
videos.w: A commenter simply flags it as a gem worth checking out.

videos.t: Bringing Out the Dead (4/9) Movie CLIP - I Be Bangin'! (1999) HD
videos.s: A scene from the 1999 film Bringing Out the Dead in which paramedics revive an overdose patient with naloxone.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a classic clip of naloxone reversing an opioid overdose.

videos.t: University Lecture: The D-Lightful Vitamin D for Health by Michael F. Holick
videos.s: A Boston University lecture by vitamin D researcher Michael Holick on vitamin D and health.
videos.w: Commenters call the speaker entertaining and cite it for explaining why sun-made vitamin D does not cause toxicity and why northern latitudes make none in winter.

videos.t: Intern’s First Order
videos.s: A Dr. Glaucomflecken skit in which a medical intern calls the hospital pharmacist about an order.
videos.w: Shared as a wholesome skit about the intern and pharmacist relationship.

videos.t: Semiología médica - Anamnesis teórica
videos.s: A Spanish-language lesson on medical history-taking (anamnesis) from Tuvi Academy.
videos.w: A student suggests it as a way to get comfortable with the patient interview in Spanish, though its vocabulary is not comprehensive.

videos.t: Nicotine’s Effects on the Brain & Body & How to Quit Smoking or Vaping
videos.s: A Huberman Lab podcast episode on nicotine's effects on the brain and body and on how to quit smoking or vaping.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for its discussion of nicotine addiction and smoking harms with linked peer-reviewed sources.

videos.t: Your Brain Hallucinates Your Conscious Reality | Anil Seth | TED
videos.s: Neuroscientist Anil Seth argues in this TED talk that perception is a controlled hallucination: the brain constantly predicts the world and our shared agreement is what we call reality. He also touches on the construction of the self.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for an example in which the same sound is heard differently depending on expectation, and for the brain as prediction machine.

videos.t: Physician Suicide Awareness 2022
videos.s: A resident-led awareness video from Harbor-UCLA Medical Center on physician mental health and suicide, made in 2022.
videos.w: Commenters share it to spread awareness of physician suicide.

videos.t: Coronavirus ‘worse than a bomb’ on Italy, says doctor coordinating response
videos.s: Channel 4 News interview with the Italian doctor coordinating the ICU response during the early COVID-19 outbreak.
videos.w: Commenters call it a frank, well-explained account of how severe and contagious COVID was compared with flu.

videos.t: Making Your Own Reusable Elastomeric Respirator For Use During Covid-19 Viral Pandemic N95 Shortage
videos.s: A surgeon demonstrates making a reusable elastomeric respirator from anesthesia supplies during the N95 shortage.
videos.w: Commenters call it a simple, ingenious N95 workaround and point to a companion video on fit testing.

videos.t: Lung Recruitment
videos.s: Short demonstration of lung recruitment and the effect of PEEP.
videos.w: A commenter calls it a cool illustration of what PEEP does.

videos.t: How to look very carefully for nystagmus by using a blank piece of paper
videos.s: A short Peter Johns demonstration of a trick using a blank sheet of paper to make nystagmus easier to see.
videos.w: A commenter shares it as a way to increase the chance of seeing nystagmus on exam.

videos.t: How to Enhance Your Gut Microbiome for Brain & Overall Health
videos.s: Huberman Lab podcast episode on the gut-brain axis and how the gut microbiome affects the nervous system, hunger and overall health. It covers the pathways by which the gut influences the brain and practical steps for gut health.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it to anyone who wants to learn about improving gut health, with a neuroscientist explaining the research so far.

videos.t: What Is Dopamine And How Does It Work In Psychosis?
videos.s: A Psychofarm video explaining what dopamine does and how it relates to psychosis and delusions.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for a deeper understanding of dopamine in psychosis, including a cognitive neuroscience view of delusions.

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1080 - David Goggins
videos.s: Joe Rogan interviews David Goggins, a retired Navy SEAL and ultramarathon runner, about his path from overweight to elite endurance athlete and pushing beyond comfort zones.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a sharper, anti-motivational take on getting outside your comfort zone.

videos.t: "The Dangerous Truth About Protein" - Janice Stanger, Ph.D.
videos.s: Presentation by Janice Stanger arguing that protein is overhyped and that excess or the wrong kinds of protein are harmful. It promotes a whole-foods, plant-based diet.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for the claim that excess protein is harmful and causes disease.

videos.t: Where Do Trees Get Their Mass?
videos.s: Veritasium asks people where a tree's mass comes from, then explains that most of a dry tree's mass comes from carbon dioxide in the air. It combines street interviews with a short explanation of photosynthesis.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a fun demonstration of how unintuitive the answer is.

videos.t: Nanobot (Havana Parody) | A Capella Science ft. Dorothy Andrusiak
videos.s: A Capella Science parody of Havana retold as a song about molecular machines and nanotechnology. It features animations of rotaxanes, catenanes and molecular switches, and comes with footnotes.
videos.w: Commenters call it a catchy edutainment song about life as molecular machines.

videos.t: Dr. Chris Knobbe - 'Diseases of Civilization: Are Seed Oil Excesses the Unifying Mechanism?'
videos.s: Ophthalmologist Chris Knobbe argues at Low Carb Denver 2020 that excess omega-6 seed oils are a unifying cause of chronic diseases of civilization such as diabetes and macular degeneration.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best talk on the health dangers of seed oils.

videos.t: How to Refract Tutorial: Jackson Cross Cylinder Technique
videos.s: An Eye Doc tutorial on subjective refraction using the Jackson cross cylinder technique.
videos.w: A technician says this older video helped them understand refraction and sharpen their skills.

videos.t: Statement of Purpose & Personal Statement: Reading Berkeley Masters of Public Health Essays & Tips
videos.s: A video in which Lauren Valdez reads Berkeley Master of Public Health essays and gives tips for writing a statement of purpose and personal statement.
videos.w: A commenter points to it as a step-by-step guide for strong public health application essays.

videos.t: Sulforaphane and Its Effects on Cancer, Mortality, Aging, Brain and Behavior, Heart Disease & More
videos.s: Rhonda Patrick makes a case for isothiocyanates such as sulforaphane from cruciferous vegetables and broccoli sprouts. It covers cancer, aging, heart disease, brain and behavior, and neurodegeneration, with chapter timestamps.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a science-backed look at the health benefits of the broccoli sprout compound, especially for cancer.

videos.t: Understanding Pain in less than 5 minutes, and what to do about it!
videos.s: A short explainer on where pain comes from and what to do about it, aimed at patients with chronic or complex pain.
videos.w: A commenter says it was useful when shown in medical school and encourages clinicians to watch it.

videos.t: Deactivate ur Brain's Selected Parts, Use Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation !!
videos.s: A video showing transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in action, from a UCL research group's demonstration.
videos.w: Commenters share it for people who have not seen TMS in action before.

videos.t: Medical Myths: Radiation | Nuffield Health
videos.s: A Nuffield Health explainer that addresses common myths about radiation exposure from medical imaging.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a quick explainer for patients worried about radiation.

videos.t: Understand Borderline Organization (Otto Kernberg and Borderline Personality Organization)
videos.s: A Psychofarm video explaining Kernberg's model of borderline personality organization, including splitting and reality testing.
videos.w: Commenters call it a great series on borderline personality and where splitting comes from.

videos.t: Dr. Marik's Vit. C Miracle Juice: Genius or Madman? | Incident Report 137
videos.s: A ZDoggMD interview with Dr. Paul Marik about the vitamin C, thiamine and steroids protocol for sepsis.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for the basic science behind the cocktail and for a skeptical host being humbled.

videos.t: Abraham Verghese: A doctor's touch
videos.s: TED Talk by Abraham Verghese on the physical exam as a ritual and the value of a doctor's touch.
videos.w: Cited as a thoughtful perspective on why the bedside exam still matters.

videos.t: David Nichols - DMT And The Pineal Gland: Facts vs Fantasy.
videos.s: A talk by pharmacologist David Nichols at Breaking Convention on DMT and the pineal gland, separating evidence from speculation.
videos.w: Commenters send it to people asking about endogenous DMT, since it shows the evidence for natural brain DMT activity is slim.

videos.t: Neuroplasticity
videos.s: A short animated explainer from Sentis on neuroplasticity and the idea that neurons that fire together wire together.
videos.w: Offered as a basic, surface-level starting point on neuroplasticity.

videos.t: Ed Boyden: A light switch for neurons
videos.s: Ed Boyden's TED talk on optogenetics, using light to switch neurons on and off.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a nice talk on optogenetics.

videos.t: Lee Cronin: Origin of Life, Aliens, Complexity, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #269
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews University of Glasgow chemist Lee Cronin about the origin of life, aliens, complexity and consciousness. The conversation centers on Cronin's assembly theory.
videos.w: Commenters say it changed their view of life and the universe, and note its discussion of detecting biotic molecules by mass spectrometry.

videos.t: EHR State of Mind | An Electronic Medical Records Parody
videos.s: Zubin parody song, EHR State of Mind, about the frustrations of electronic medical records.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives a good sense of the drawbacks of EHR systems that clinicians find frustrating.

videos.t: Growing Living Rat Neurons To Play... DOOM? | Part 1
videos.s: The Thought Emporium grows living rat neurons on an electrode array and tries to train them to play Doom. It is part of a series on biological computing.
videos.w: Commenters recommend the channel for its range of topics and cite the series as an example of neurons on a chip.

videos.t: Positive Predictive Value & Disease Prevalence
videos.s: A Medmastery explainer on positive predictive value and disease prevalence, a worked example of Bayesian reasoning for test results.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good explanation of test sensitivity and predictive value.

videos.t: 5 Cases in 5 Minutes: Thoracic #1
videos.s: A Radquarters short from the 5 Cases in 5 Minutes series, a thoracic imaging case featuring crazy paving and pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.
videos.w: A commenter lists Radquarters among three recommended radiology teaching channels.

videos.t: The Nervous System, Part 1: Crash Course Anatomy & Physiology #8
videos.s: Part 1 of CrashCourse's nervous system episodes in its Anatomy & Physiology series, covering the basic anatomy of the nervous system.
videos.w: Commenters say it covers the topic at a level a non-biology background can follow.

videos.t: Gambling and the desire machine | Pay to Win
videos.s: A 70-minute video essay by Jimmy McGee on gambling, addiction and game design, tracing horse racing, slot machines and collectible card markets. It is the first in a series on making money from games.
videos.w: Commenters call it an interesting exploration of the murky history of video games and gambling and of why gambling machines appeal.

videos.t: Memories are Made of This
videos.s: A lecture by Nobel laureate Eric Kandel on the molecular basis of memory, including his work on CREB and long-term potentiation.
videos.w: Commenters call it an intro-level lecture from Kandel himself and a good revision of his CREB and LTP work, though somewhat outdated.

videos.t: First Day of Pathology
videos.s: A Dr. Glaucomflecken comedy skit about a first day in pathology, portraying a physician switching into the specialty.
videos.w: A commenter calls it one of the most realistic portrayals of pathologists they have seen.

videos.t: Am I still lactose tolerant? - Lactose Gene Therapy Update
videos.s: The Thought Emporium's update on the home-brewed gene therapy he took to cure his lactose intolerance. It reports how the effect held up over two years and what future versions might look like.
videos.w: Commenters follow it as an update on the DIY lactose gene therapy self-experiment and as cool home biology work.

videos.t: Ultrasound-guided peripheral venous cannulation
videos.s: An InterAnest video demonstrating ultrasound-guided peripheral venous cannulation with the in-plane technique.
