videos.w: Commenters call it very useful in obese patients whose veins can be neither seen nor felt.

videos.t: The Glass Spine
videos.s: A demonstration from OAAinfo using a glass model of the spine to show how injected drug spreads in the subarachnoid space with position and baricity.
videos.w: Anesthesia commenters call it really useful for showing how drugs move in the subarachnoid space.

videos.t: Split brain behavioral experiments
videos.s: A video on split-brain behavioral experiments, based on Gazzaniga's research on patients with a severed corpus callosum.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a way to see the effects of a severed corpus callosum and Gazzaniga's split-brain work.

videos.t: Do we see reality as it is? | Donald Hoffman | TED
videos.s: Cognitive scientist Donald Hoffman argues in a TED talk that evolution shaped perception to track fitness rather than truth. He uses evolutionary simulations and the Australian jewel beetle as examples.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for the idea that perception works like a user illusion rather than showing reality as it is.

videos.t: The Biggest Chemical Coverup In History
videos.s: Veritasium investigates PFAS forever chemicals, from the history of Teflon to pollution of the global water system and their presence in the US population. It covers the corporate cover-up and the host's own blood tests.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a good explanation of PFAS and their very low safe limits, and one stopped eating microwave popcorn after it.

videos.t: Robert Sapolsky: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst
videos.s: A 73-minute Stanford talk by Robert Sapolsky drawn from his book Behave. It surveys the biological factors behind human behavior at its best and worst.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as an example of Sapolsky's storytelling-driven lecturing on physical and environmental influences on human actions.

videos.t: Change Your Brain: Neuroscientist Dr. Andrew Huberman | Rich Roll Podcast
videos.s: A Rich Roll Podcast conversation with neuroscientist Andrew Huberman on changing your brain, including dopamine and motivation.
videos.w: Commenters say he breaks down dopamine and goal-setting well, with the useful part starting at about the 27-minute mark.

videos.t: Integrated Information Theory   explained
videos.s: An explainer introducing the Integrated Information Theory of consciousness.
videos.w: Commenters call it a fairly good introduction, though it assumes some formal logic.

videos.t: Opioids II: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: John Oliver's second Last Week Tonight segment on the opioid epidemic, covering the role of large companies in driving it, including Purdue Pharma and the Sackler family.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as one of three Oliver segments that explain how pharma marketing drove US opioid prescribing.

videos.t: Principles of Natural Running with Dr. Mark Cucuzzella
videos.s: Short instructional video in which Dr. Mark Cucuzzella of the Natural Running Center describes the principles of good running technique, including barefoot-style mechanics.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best video they have seen on natural running form, with useful tips on technique.

videos.t: God is in The Neurons
videos.s: A short documentary on how identity, culture, religion and emotion are tied to the brain.
videos.w: Shared as an interesting short documentary on neuroscience and the nature of emotions.

videos.t: COVID-19 Vaccines: MODERNA | PFIZER/BIONTECH | ASTRAZENECA
videos.s: Ninja Nerd whiteboard lecture on the Moderna, Pfizer/BioNTech and AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccines. It covers how each works, the preclinical and phase I-III trial process, and Operation Warp Speed.
videos.w: One commenter calls it the best science-based video on how the different COVID vaccines work, with technical detail on mRNA vaccines and trials.

videos.t: Loneliness
videos.s: Kurzgesagt explains why humans feel loneliness, its evolutionary role, and how modern life can turn it into a harmful downward spiral. It cites research and offers ideas on what to do about it.
videos.w: Commenters call it an excellent, research-backed summary of loneliness that treats it like a symptom, such as hunger.

videos.t: 327 - Choices, costs, and challenges in US healthcare: insurance, drug pricing, & potential reforms
videos.s: Peter Attia podcast in which Tenet Healthcare CEO Saum Sutaria walks through the structure and financial flows of the US healthcare system. They cover insurance, drug pricing, how the system evolved and possible reforms.
videos.w: Commenters call it the best primer on the choices that make US healthcare expensive and where the money goes.

videos.t: Dr Russell Barkley on ADHD Meds and how they all work differently from each other
videos.s: Short clip in which Russell Barkley explains how different ADHD medications work and how they differ from one another.
videos.w: Commenters say Barkley gives good explanations of what the various prescription ADHD drugs do.

videos.t: The Neuroanatomy of ADHD and thus how to treat ADHD - CADDAC - Dr Russel Barkley part 3ALL
videos.s: Russell Barkley lectures on the neuroanatomy of ADHD and how to treat it, linking executive function and working memory to the disorder. It is part 3 of a CADDAC series.
videos.w: One commenter says it helped them put their behaviors in perspective and understand how their brain works, and others find it more detailed than typical tips.

videos.t: How to recover from depression
videos.s: Clinical psychologist Michael Yapko draws on forty years of practice and research to explain skills that help people recover from, and even prevent, depression. He stresses cognitive and social factors beyond medication.
videos.w: Commenters call it a comprehensive, multidimensional view of depression, and one says it helped them immensely.

videos.t: The Obesity Code Lecture (Why do we get Fat?) Part 1
videos.s: Jason Fung lecture on why obesity became an epidemic since the 1970s, arguing that insulin and hormones rather than calories drive weight gain. He explains why calorie counting fails and touches on low-carb eating and fasting.
videos.w: Commenters call his explanation of obesity compelling and cite the argument that insulin, not calories, drives long-term weight gain.

videos.t: Long Term Potentiation and Memory Formation, Animation
videos.s: A narrated animation from Alila Medical Media on how long-term potentiation strengthens synapses in the hippocampus and underlies memory formation.
videos.w: Commenters in a neuroscience thread point to it as a clear explanation of LTP and the basics of learning and memory pathways.

videos.t: D is for Debacle - The Crucial Story of Vitamin D and Human Health
videos.s: Ivor Cummins gives an 82-minute presentation on the history and science of vitamin D and human health. He draws on expert interviews to argue that sun exposure and vitamin D status are linked to many chronic diseases.
videos.w: Commenters call it well worth watching in full and cite its case that vitamin D supplementation is underappreciated.

videos.t: Michael Levin: Anatomical decision-making by cellular collectives
videos.s: Michael Levin presents his lab's work on how cellular collectives use bioelectric networks to make anatomical decisions. Topics include pattern memories, regeneration and synthetic living organisms.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as an overview of Levin's work on bioelectric control of anatomy, including planaria that regenerate after being split.

videos.t: Awake through brain surgery (1 of 3)
videos.s: Footage of a patient undergoing brain surgery while awake, the first of a three-part series from the Aleph Zero channel. It shows the operation as it happens.
videos.w: Viewers share it as striking footage of a patient who is awake during brain surgery.

videos.t: 23. Language
videos.s: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford lecture on language, comparing human and animal communication, ape language projects such as Koko and Kanzi, and how language is acquired. It is part of his human behavioral biology course.
videos.w: Commenters recommend the whole course for understanding how the brain works, and this lecture covers ape language and how the brain encodes second languages.

videos.t: pinky and the brain-brainstem
videos.s: A light-hearted video that uses a Pinky and the Brain theme to teach the structure of the brainstem.
videos.w: Commenters say it makes neuroanatomy bearable and helps relax and engage students in a lecture.

videos.t: Antibody ID: The Basics (Part 1)
videos.ch: Blood Bank Guy (D. Joe Chaffin MD)
videos.s: The first part of a blood bank series by a transfusion medicine physician on the basics of antibody identification.
videos.w: A lab professional points to it as the bare-essentials start from a well-organized series that works as a refresher.

videos.t: Allegories on race and racism | Camara Jones | TEDxEmory
videos.s: A TEDxEmory talk by Camara Jones using allegories, including a gardener's story, to explain institutionalized racism and social determinants of health.
videos.w: Commenters say her metaphors explain social determinants of health and racism especially well.

videos.t: NRMP Match Algorithm Explained (Residency Application Process)
videos.s: A Med School Insiders explainer of how the NRMP Match algorithm assigns applicants to residency programs.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for understanding how residency matching works and why it was created.

videos.t: Ditching Naturopathy for Real Science (w/ Britt Hermes)
videos.s: An interview with Britt Hermes, a former naturopath who left the field, discussing what she saw in naturopathic practice.
videos.w: Commenters found her account of naturopathy's practices and dangers disturbing and worth hearing.

videos.t: FACT POLICE: Residency applicants and residency positions
videos.s: Sheriff of Sodium video fact-checking claims about US residency applicants, residency positions and the Match.
videos.w: Commenters say it clarifies the actual numbers around residency spots.

videos.t: Anatomy for Beginners - Lesson 1: Movement
videos.s: Lesson 1, on movement, of Gunther von Hagens Anatomy for Beginners, a gross anatomy lecture series using cadavers and live models.
videos.w: Commenters call it gruesome but incredibly interesting and a well-done anatomy series.

videos.t: Spider vs Penis (Priapism) - Smarter Every Day 98
videos.s: A Smarter Every Day episode on priapism caused by the bite of the Brazilian wandering spider.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an entertaining video on a real toxicology and physiology topic.

videos.t: The Most Radioactive Places on Earth
videos.s: A Veritasium video on the most radioactive places on Earth, comparing radiation levels with everyday references such as bananas.
videos.w: Commenters in radiology point to it for its banana-scale comparison of radiation doses.

videos.t: Fluoride in the Water Isn't Going to Hurt You
videos.s: A Healthcare Triage video arguing that water fluoridation is safe and reviewing the evidence behind it.
videos.w: Commenters like it as a comprehensive summary of the scientific consensus on fluoride.

videos.t: Picornavirus Overview - SketchyMicro (USMLE Microbiology Review)
videos.s: A Sketchy Learning USMLE video on picornaviruses, using illustrated mnemonic stories to teach microbiology.
videos.w: Students recommend the visual stories for memorizing advanced micro and pharm material in an entertaining way.

videos.t: Reduce Anxiety & Stress with the Physiological Sigh | Huberman Lab Quantal Clip
videos.s: A Huberman Lab clip on the physiological sigh, a breathing technique to reduce anxiety and stress.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives the science behind the technique and that it works and is easy to do.

videos.t: Blood Supply of Brain | Circle of Willis | Part 1/11
videos.s: Part 1 of an 11-part Dr. Najeeb lecture series on the blood supply of the brain, including the circle of Willis.
videos.w: Students say the lectures make cerebral blood flow clearer and help neuroanatomy stick through repetition.

videos.t: Easy Coagulation Cascade (1 of 2) - Simple & easy to remember
videos.s: First of a two-part series condensing the coagulation cascade into an easy schematic.
videos.w: Commenters say the series helped them understand and remember the cascade.

videos.t: Exponential growth and epidemics
videos.s: A short 3Blue1Brown primer on exponential and logistic growth, using early COVID-19 case data to show how epidemics grow and eventually level off. It explains why small changes in growth rate make enormous differences.
videos.w: Commenters say it puts pandemic spread in perspective for any viewer and explains the logistic curve of epidemics.

videos.t: Neurology | Neuron Anatomy & Function
videos.s: A Ninja Nerd lecture on neuron anatomy and function.
videos.w: Students find the Ninja Nerd neuroanatomy videos, including this one, helpful for the basics.

videos.t: Anki: How to Find Cards and Tags in the Browser
videos.s: The AnKing video on finding cards and tags in the Anki browser.
videos.w: Commenters say the search method helps find cards by resource.

videos.t: Don't Use UWorld Without Watching This!
videos.s: LY Med video on using UWorld as a learning tool rather than a test of readiness.
videos.w: Commenters say it calmed them and reminds students not to be discouraged by UWorld percentages.

videos.t: Anki Med School Basics 1
videos.s: The first video in a series on learning Anki for medical school, covering the software and cloze cards.
videos.w: Students say the series explains Anki and cloze cards well and was super helpful when starting.

videos.t: Joscha: From Computation to Consciousness (31c3)
videos.s: Joscha Bach's 31c3 talk arguing the mind can be understood as an information-processing system, touring the philosophy behind AI and cognitive science.
videos.w: Mentioned by a Hacker News reader as an example of the Joscha Bach talks they enjoy.

videos.t: Growing Human Neurons on a Home Made Electrode Array
videos.s: The Thought Emporium builds a homemade multi-electrode array, grows human neurons on it and tries to take readings. It is the first part of a series aimed at connecting living neurons to a computer.
videos.w: Commenters like it as a hobbyist replicating neurons-on-a-chip work from a garage.

videos.t: How to Pass USMLE STEP1 in 8 weeks
videos.s: A first-person account of preparing for USMLE Step 1 in eight weeks, explaining a 12-week prep plan.
videos.w: A commenter found it motivating, from someone who raised NBME scores in six weeks.

videos.t: Kinesin protein walking on microtubule
videos.s: A very short animation of a kinesin motor protein walking along a microtubule inside a cell while carrying cargo.
videos.w: Commenters like it as a quick, cartoon-like picture of how protein machines move cargo in cells, including kinesin and dynein.

videos.t: The Amboss Anki Add-on and How to Customize It
videos.s: The AnKing video on setting up and customizing the AMBOSS add-on for Anki.
videos.w: Users say it gives the basic idea of using the add-on, though it may be dated.

videos.t: High Yield USMLE/COMLEX Images (pt. 2)
videos.s: Part 2 of Dirty Medicine's high-yield USMLE and COMLEX image review, pairing images with exam buzzwords.
videos.w: A commenter says the buzzwords and images earned a few points on the exam.

videos.t: Anki for Med School: Using Cloze Deletion Cards
videos.s: Tutorial on making cloze deletion cards in Anki for medical school.
videos.w: Students say it helped them learn how to build cloze cards.

videos.t: "How do I review the NBMEs in final month?"
videos.s: Mehlman Medical explains how to review NBME practice exams in the final month before the USMLE.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for how to learn from NBME practice forms.

videos.t: High Yield Pulmonology Review for Step 1 - Pt 1 (Lung Development and Physiology)
videos.s: Part 1 of a high-yield pulmonology review for Step 1, covering lung development and physiology.
videos.w: Students say it gives the basics to build flashcards on and helped them survive the pulmonology block.

videos.t: Easy Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Mnemonic
videos.s: Two-minute mnemonic video on the pathway of congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
videos.w: Students use it to reason through CAH questions, though one notes an error about 11-hydroxylase.

videos.t: Coagulation Cascade || USMLE
videos.s: Dirty Medicine mnemonic video for the coagulation cascade.
videos.w: Students say the mnemonic makes the pathway easy to remember.

videos.t: Sodium Channel Blockers - Easy Pharm for USMLE Step 1
videos.s: A three-minute Pharm 450 video on class I sodium channel blocker antiarrhythmics for USMLE Step 1.
videos.w: Students say the sketchy-style video covers the basics of class I drugs and helped before a cardiology test.

videos.t: Preparing your CV for Residency Applications
videos.s: A video from The AnKing on preparing a CV for residency applications, with a template in the description.
videos.w: Students used the template and found the structuring advice helpful.

videos.t: Why Do We Fall - Motivational Video
videos.s: Motivational video from Mateusz M about why we fall, used by students preparing for Step 1.
videos.w: Commenters say it captures the mindset needed for Step 1 and helped them through a dark time.

videos.t: Why Everybody is Misusing The First Aid for the USMLE
videos.s: A video on how to use First Aid for the USMLE efficiently, treating it as a checklist rather than something to annotate heavily.
videos.w: A commenter says it explains efficient study methods better than annotating.

videos.t: COMPLETE Ethics & Law (for USMLE & COMLEX) - with 100+ questions!!
videos.s: AJmonics runs through ethics and law for USMLE and COMLEX with over 100 practice questions.
videos.w: Commenters call it the fastest way to pick up extra points when time is short.

videos.t: Ron Vale (UCSF, HHMI) 1: Molecular Motor Proteins
videos.s: Ron Vale of UCSF and HHMI gives an introductory lecture on kinesin, dynein and myosin motor proteins. He covers their roles in cells and how they turn ATP hydrolysis into directed motion and force.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as an explanation of how protein motors walk along microtubules and an example of how strange cellular machinery is.

videos.t: Heart Murmurs
videos.s: A Strong Medicine lecture on heart murmurs and bruits.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a good deep dive and a free alternative to paid heart sound resources.

videos.t: Guide to using Divine Intervention Podcasts | New USMLE Step 2 CK | USMLE November changes
videos.s: A video guide on how to use the Divine Intervention podcasts for USMLE Step 2 CK preparation, made around a Step 2 format change.
videos.w: A commenter recommends it for suggested extra episodes to listen to.

videos.t: Auditory Transduction (2002)
videos.s: Brandon Pletsch animated explanation of auditory transduction and how air conduction of sound works.
videos.w: Students call it a great summary of the auditory system.

videos.t: ERAS and Financial Conflict of Interest at the AAMC
videos.s: Sheriff of Sodium video on ERAS and financial conflict of interest at the AAMC.
videos.w: Commenters call it a thought-provoking treatment from a strong medical student advocate.

videos.t: How I got 265 on USMLE Step 1 (Study schedule, How to solve questions, high yield topics,Test day)
videos.s: A first-person account of scoring 265 on USMLE Step 1, covering the study schedule, how to approach questions, high-yield topics and test day.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives a complete overview and good advice on structuring a three-month study plan.

videos.t: The Hyperbolic Geometry of DMT Experiences (@Harvard Science of Psychedelics Club)
videos.s: A Qualia Research Institute lecture given to a Harvard psychedelics club, modelling DMT experiences with hyperbolic geometry and dynamical systems. It links intoxication level to changes in the curvature and information content of experience.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a lecture with a good intro to hyperbolic geometry as applied to DMT visuals.

videos.t: Introduction to Direct and Indirect Inguinal Hernia
videos.s: An Armando Hasudungan illustrated introduction to direct and indirect inguinal hernias and their anatomy.
videos.w: Students say it helped them understand and visualize the anatomy of hernias.

videos.t: Retina exam on slit lamp - COMPLETE GUIDE
videos.s: A complete guide to examining the retina at the slit lamp with a handheld lens, from the Learn About Eyes channel. It is aimed at those learning the technique.
videos.w: Ophthalmology learners call it the best video they found for learning indirect ophthalmoscopy and the 90D lens exam.

videos.t: CFI04: Advice from Dr. Fischer:  Which USMLE step is most important?
videos.s: A video of advice from Conrad Fischer on which USMLE step matters most, aimed at international medical graduates applying for residency.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for its advice from a residency program director and for applicants hoping to recover from a weak result.

videos.t: F*ck That: An Honest Meditation
videos.s: A humorous guided meditation by Jason Headley that swears its way through the usual meditation script.
videos.w: Commenters say it helps skeptics get past the mental block and is a funny way to unwind before sleep.

videos.t: Pass the PSA: Prescribing Skills Assessment for finals
videos.s: MedSchoolHacks video on preparing for the UK Prescribing Skills Assessment taken in final year.
videos.w: Commenters say it helps anyone sitting the PSA soon.

videos.t: ABG Interpretation: Compensation and Mixed Disorders (Lesson 4)
videos.s: Strong Medicine lesson on ABG interpretation, compensation and mixed acid-base disorders.
videos.w: Commenters like the Winter's formula shortcut for estimating compensation at the bedside.

videos.t: The Medical H and P (Part 1 of 2)
videos.s: Part 1 of a two-part Strong Medicine series on the medical history and physical and how to present a case.
videos.w: Students say the series helped with structure and what to include or leave out in presentations.

videos.t: How to Diagnose the Sacrum Part 1
videos.s: A video on diagnosing the sacrum in osteopathic manipulative medicine, part 1 of a series from LMU-DCOM fellows.
videos.w: Osteopathic students call it clutch for OMM sacral questions and a helpful technique video.

videos.t: The Predictive Accuracy of NBME Forms 25-30, UWSA-1, & UWSA-2
videos.s: An Elite Medical Prep analysis of how predictive NBME forms 25-30 and UWSA-1 and UWSA-2 are of real exam scores.
videos.w: Commenters found it accurate on how each form over- or underestimates scores.

videos.t: Step 2 CS - Blue Sheet
videos.s: A Dr. Laura Miranda video on the Step 2 CS blue sheet, a system for structuring the patient encounter.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a good system to learn last minute and they used her method.

videos.t: The Immune System Explained I – Bacteria Infection
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animation showing how the immune system responds to a bacterial infection, with immune cells depicted as an army defending the body.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a simple layman's introduction to the steps of the immune response.

videos.t: How to Submit ERAS Without Screwing it Up
videos.s: A video on how to submit the ERAS residency application and avoid common mistakes.
videos.w: Students point to it for common ERAS errors and the certify versus assign distinction.

videos.t: Cardiac Arrhythmias | Atrial & Ventricular | Tachycardia & Bradycardia🫀
videos.s: A Dr. Najeeb lecture on atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, covering tachycardias and bradycardias in detail.
videos.w: Commenters call it high-yield and well explained, though long and time-consuming.

videos.t: Anki: Making Effective Cards
videos.s: The AnKing explains what makes a self-made Anki card effective.

videos.t: Core Ethical Principles (Part 1)
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video covering core ethical principles for medical students.

videos.t: Medicare vs. Medicaid | Mnemonic for USMLE
videos.s: A Pixorize mnemonic video explaining the differences between Medicare and Medicaid for USMLE.

videos.t: Memorize Lists Effectively with Cloze Overlapper for Anki
videos.s: Tutorial on the Cloze Overlapper add-on for Anki to memorize ordered lists.

videos.t: Anki Add-on Guide: Gamify Your Reviews
videos.s: Glutanimate guide to Anki add-ons that gamify reviews.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a way to make Anki reviews more game-like.

videos.t: Lysosomal Storage Diseases (Sphingolipidoses) MADE EASY with mnemonics!
videos.s: A BabyStepMED video teaching the lysosomal storage diseases (sphingolipidoses) with mnemonics.
videos.w: Commenters call the mnemonics awesome and amazing for these diseases.

videos.t: Signaling Pathways of Endocrine Hormones First Aid USMLE Step 1
videos.s: A TheMed Tutor video on signaling pathways of endocrine hormones, following the First Aid USMLE Step 1 material.

videos.t: Top Biohacks to Score 260+ on USMLE
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine video of test-day tips for the USMLE, including exercise and sleep advice.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for its test-day habits and encouragement.

videos.t: Anki: How to Customize Background, Gears, Text & More!
videos.s: The AnKing video on customizing Anki background, gears and text with add-ons.
videos.w: Users point to it for installing and using the background add-on.

videos.t: Homochirality: Why Nature Never Makes Mirror Molecules
videos.s: Steve Mould explains homochirality, the reason biological molecules such as sugars and amino acids come in only one handedness. He covers ideas about how this asymmetry arose, touching on meteorite samples and RNA.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a clear explanation of why life makes only one version of its molecules.

videos.t: How to write ERAS residency personal statement
videos.s: A guide to writing an ERAS residency personal statement, presented for diagnostic radiology.
videos.w: Students say the structure and tailoring advice apply to any specialty.

videos.t: Heart Embryology Animation
videos.s: Animation of embryologic heart development by Stella Seppings.
videos.w: A student says a professor had them watch it, and others say it made cardio and neuro easy to understand.

videos.t: Clinical testing extraocular muscles tutorial
videos.s: The Noted Anatomist tutorial on clinically testing the extraocular muscles and ocular motility.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good explanation of eye muscle movements from a creator with other clinical anatomy videos.

videos.t: How to Analyze & Review an NBME | #USMLE Step 1 & 2 CK (part 2)
videos.s: Rahul Damania presents a system for analyzing and reviewing NBME practice exams, part 2.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for a method of reviewing incorrect answers from NBME and CMS forms.

videos.t: How To Set Up, Update, and Use AnKing Step 2 Deck for Clinical Rotations | Simple M3 Workflow
videos.s: A video guide to installing, updating and using the AnKing Step 2 deck and tags for clinical rotations.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for a detailed explanation of using Anki with the AnKing deck during clerkships.

videos.t: My Daily Workflow for Medical School - What Works
videos.s: Zach Highley describes his daily study workflow in medical school.
videos.w: Students find the routine inspiring for getting started in med school.

videos.t: Medical Residency Applications Advice Tips from Program Directors
videos.s: A video with advice from program directors on how residency applications are reviewed and what applicants should do.
videos.w: Commenters call it helpful, blunt advice and a good look at how application review works.

videos.t: Tiny Bombs in your Blood - The Complement System
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animation explaining the complement system of the immune response.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives an easy overview of a difficult topic, though not in great detail.

videos.t: ECFMG step by step Registration Process
videos.s: A step-by-step walkthrough of the ECFMG registration process for international medical graduates taking USMLE.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains everything for IMGs and clears up confusion about registration.

videos.t: Cordyceps: attack of the killer fungi - Planet Earth Attenborough BBC wildlife
videos.s: Three-minute clip from BBC's Planet Earth narrated by David Attenborough about Cordyceps, the fungus that infects insects and takes over their behavior. It shows an infected ant and its demise.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a short introduction to cordyceps fungi and how they control ant behavior.

videos.t: How The Immune System ACTUALLY Works – IMMUNE
videos.s: Kurzgesagt animation giving a big-picture tour of the human immune system, its organs, transport network, and the cells it produces every day. It accompanies their IMMUNE book.
videos.w: Commenters like the series for explaining the immune system's complexity simply.

videos.t: Draw the Brachial Plexus in 10 seconds!
videos.s: A chiropractor demonstrates how to draw the brachial plexus in about ten seconds.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a quick way to draw the plexus and was unbelievably helpful for the upper extremity.

videos.t: ADHD & How Anyone Can Improve Their Focus
videos.s: Andrew Huberman discusses ADHD, its biology and myths, behavioral and drug treatments, and training protocols to improve focus for people with or without ADHD. It covers dopamine and coordination of brain networks.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as advice on ADHD and focus from a credentialed source, including the point that some brain areas are desynchronized in ADHD.

videos.t: How to make an Anki card deck using Microsoft Excel
videos.s: Tutorial on building an Anki deck from a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet and importing it.
videos.w: Commenters say it helped them learn to import cards into Anki.

videos.t: Why Life Seems to Speed Up as We Age
videos.s: Veritasium explores why time seems to speed up as we age, covering chronoception and several competing explanations beyond the common proportional-theory argument.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains the effect in detail and offers more compelling alternatives than the usual argument.

videos.t: High Yield CT Scans (Part 1) || USMLE
videos.s: The first part of Dirty Medicine's high-yield CT scan review for USMLE, going through classic images to recognize.
videos.w: Step 1 studiers call the high-yield imaging videos a must-watch.

videos.t: How to use Anki filter decks during dedicated USMLE STEP 1 studying
videos.s: A tutorial on using Anki filtered decks during dedicated USMLE Step 1 study.
videos.w: Commenters used it to learn how to make a filtered deck.

videos.t: The Mind - Motivational Video
videos.s: Motivational video from Mateusz M called The Mind, aimed at students studying for exams.
videos.w: A commenter says these motivational videos gave them drive for studying.

videos.t: Endocrinology | Receptor Pathways
videos.s: A Ninja Nerd lecture on endocrinology receptor pathways, including Gs, Gi and Gq signaling.
videos.w: Step 1 studiers say it explains signaling well, though it is slow enough to watch at 2x.

videos.t: USMLE STEP 1: ETHICS (PART 1) w/ Questions
videos.s: A Randy Neil video on ethics for USMLE Step 1, part 1, with practice questions.
videos.w: Students say Randy Neil plus UWorld is probably enough for ethics, and he covers communication questions too.

videos.t: Your Body Killed Cancer 5 Minutes Ago
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animation on how the immune system constantly detects and kills cells that turn cancerous. It explains what cancer cells are and why stopping them is so hard.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good, simple introduction to how cancer grows and how the immune system deals with it.

videos.t: DNA & RNA Viruses Names Mnemonic
videos.s: A MedSurvival Mnemonics video giving memory aids for the lists of DNA viruses, and positive- and negative-sense RNA viruses.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a way to memorize virus lists easily for Step 1.

videos.t: Acid/Base || USMLE
videos.s: A Dirty Medicine USMLE video on acid-base disorders.
videos.w: Students say it makes acid-base easy and helped them solve every acid-base problem.

videos.t: Medical School Pathology, Chapter 1a
videos.s: A pathology course series working through Robbins pathology chapter by chapter in a high-yield format.
videos.w: Commenters suggest it for anyone learning pathology or histology.

videos.t: Craig Ferguson Speaks From The Heart
videos.s: Clip of Craig Ferguson's late-night monologue in which he talks about his past as an alcoholic. He explains why he will not mock Britney Spears over her breakdown.
videos.w: Commenters say his comments on alcoholism are worth hearing and helpful for explaining the condition to others.

videos.t: Real-time Collaboration on Anki with AnkiHub
videos.s: Short AnKing video explaining AnkiHub and real-time collaboration on Anki decks.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a one-minute answer to what AnkiHub is.

videos.t: Surgical Knot Tying: Two-handed, Righty
videos.s: A Dr. Omedary demonstration of two-handed surgical knot tying, right-handed.
videos.w: Commenters say it teaches the basic two-hand tie and its variations and shows what knot you are actually tying.

videos.t: Why We Sleep: Science of Sleep & Dreams | Matthew Walker | Talks at Google
videos.s: Berkeley sleep scientist Matthew Walker presents the science of sleep and dreams and how sleep affects health and lifespan, based on his book Why We Sleep.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a good alternative to the book, covering the effects of sleep deprivation beyond Alzheimer's.

videos.t: EKG Interpretation | Master Fundamentals of ECG | Electrocardiography
videos.s: A Dr. Najeeb lecture series on ECG fundamentals, running about three hours.
videos.w: Students and nurses say the long lectures give real understanding for people who like learning by video.

videos.t: Find your primal posture and sit without back pain: Esther Gokhale at TEDxStanford
videos.s: Esther Gokhale's short TEDx talk argues that the natural human spine is curved rather than straight and teaches a primal posture for sitting without back pain.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains why a curved spine posture can be better and that it helped with lower back and leg problems.

videos.t: Study LESS, Study SMART – What I Wish I Knew in College
videos.s: Med School Insiders video on study methods emphasizing spaced repetition and active quizzing.
videos.w: Commenters find the channel helpful for study approaches.

videos.t: How To Study USMLE Questions FAST
videos.s: Santiago AQ on how to review USMLE practice questions faster by sorting them by difficulty.
videos.w: Commenters say it improved how they review practice questions.

videos.t: Anki: Hierarchical Tags (Echelon and Better Tags)
videos.s: The AnKing video on hierarchical tags in Anki, including the Echelon and Better Tags add-ons.
videos.w: Users point to it for organizing decks and finding cards with hierarchical tags.

videos.t: A Summary of the NBME Question Writer Guide | Understand the USMLE Step 1 (*inspirational ending*)
videos.s: Rahul Damania summarizes the NBME question writer guide to show how USMLE questions are constructed.
videos.w: A commenter says it helped them understand how NBME question writers think.

videos.t: Why is it so Easy to be Thin in Japan?
videos.s: A creator compares the food environment of the US, with roughly 30 percent obesity, to Japan, at around 3.5 percent. He argues that what is available and normal to eat explains much of the gap.
videos.w: Commenters say it gives an accurate picture of everyday eating in Japan and contrasts it with the US food environment.

videos.t: How to Change Note Type in Anki
videos.s: Anki in Minutes tutorial on changing note type in bulk.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains exactly how to change note types.

videos.t: Intention to Treat
videos.s: A Sketchy EBM video explaining intention-to-treat analysis versus other trial analyses with a numeric example and visuals.
videos.w: Students say the numbers and visuals finally made the topic click.

videos.t: Medical Mystery Solved – A Diagnostic Sequence | NEJM
videos.s: NEJM Group video walking through a diagnostic sequence that solves a medical mystery.
videos.w: A commenter says NEJM makes fantastic explanatory videos on confusing clinical cases.

videos.t: USMLE DOMINATION: HIGH YIELD TUTORIAL #7- Neonatal Lung Disease
videos.s: Dr. Omer Awan's high-yield tutorial on neonatal lung disease, with radiology images, from his USMLE Domination series.
videos.w: Commenters call it a great summary of neonatal lung disease and say the channel's radiology explanations are helpful.

videos.t: Functional Anatomy of the Hand
videos.s: A vintage film on the functional anatomy of the hand, hosted on the Stanford Clinical Anatomy channel.
videos.w: A commenter calls it the coolest anatomy video they have seen.

videos.t: The Scariest Episode Yet - Still Untitled: The Adam Savage Project - 10/30/18
videos.s: An episode of Adam Savage's Still Untitled podcast with molecular biologist Joe DeRisi. They discuss his work, including sequencing blood to detect rare infections, and stories such as brain-eating amoebas.
videos.w: Commenters call his stories fascinating, especially the sequencing approach to finding rare infections.

videos.t: How Sugar & Processed Foods Impact Your Health | Dr. Robert Lustig
videos.s: A long Huberman Lab podcast episode with Dr. Robert Lustig on calories in versus calories out, and how sugar, fructose, fiber and processed foods affect insulin, liver and metabolic health.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a long talk arguing that sugar is as toxic as alcohol.

videos.t: Why Gifted Kids Are Actually Special Needs
videos.s: Dr. K of HealthyGamerGG argues that gifted kids can be seen as special needs, tracing a path from the gifted label to burnout and perfectionism.
videos.w: Commenters say it explains the emotional challenges of gifted kids, including boredom at school and struggling in college.

videos.t: Maximizing Productivity, Physical & Mental Health with Daily Tools
videos.s: A long Huberman Lab episode laying out science-based daily tools for focus, sleep, exercise and mental and physical health, organized around a 24-hour day.
videos.w: Commenters say they followed its tools for sleep, morning walks and circadian timing, and credit them with helping recovery from burnout.

videos.t: How Your Brain Works & Changes
videos.s: Andrew Huberman introduces how the nervous system produces sensation, emotion and behavior, and how neuroplasticity lets us change it. It covers neurons, synapses, brain chemicals and the rhythms behind focus, learning and sleep.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for why frustration during learning drives neural change, and for the science of sleep and multitasking.

videos.t: "Understanding Burnout," Prof. Christina Maslach (U.C. Berkeley)
videos.s: A Berkeley lecture by psychologist Christina Maslach, a leading burnout researcher, on what burnout is and what causes it. It covers common misunderstandings and the job and workplace factors involved.
videos.w: Commenters call it an expert primer that dispels most misunderstandings about burnout.

videos.t: Amputee Makes History with APL’s Modular Prosthetic Limb
videos.s: Johns Hopkins APL shows Les Baugh, a bilateral shoulder-level amputee, controlling two Modular Prosthetic Limbs by thought after a short training period. Nerves rerouted to his chest drive the arms.
videos.w: Commenters call it an impressive glimpse of thought-controlled prosthetics and how rerouted nerves can drive them.

videos.t: Strange answers to the psychopath test | Jon Ronson | TED
videos.s: Jon Ronson, author of The Psychopath Test, gives a TED talk on the blurry line between sane and crazy and on psychopathy as a spectrum, with stories of how the label gets applied.
videos.w: Commenters call it one of the best non-technical talks and cite it for the idea that psychopathy lies on a spectrum.

videos.t: Keynote - Karen Sandler
videos.s: Karen Sandler's keynote at Linux.conf.au 2012 on the software running inside medical devices such as her own pacemaker-defibrillator. She discusses how hard it is to learn what code runs in life-sustaining devices and why open source matters there.
videos.w: Commenters describe it as an excellent talk on security and bugs in the software inside your body.

videos.t: Matter to Mind:Bioelectricity, Body Intelligence, Future of Regenerative Medicine- Dr. Michael Levin
videos.s: Developmental biologist Michael Levin speaks at a Harvard Extension student event on bioelectricity, body intelligence and regenerative medicine. He discusses how electrical networks among cells guide growth and form.
videos.w: Commenters recommend his lectures as fascinating, including work on regrowing limbs by manipulating cell electrical networks.

videos.t: The Man Who Took LSD and Changed The World
videos.s: Veritasium tells the story of Kary Mullis, who invented PCR and won a Nobel Prize, and explains how PCR works and how it was developed at Cetus.
videos.w: Commenters call it one of the most accessible videos on PCR, covering taq polymerase and the origin of the technique.

videos.t: Free Energy Principle — Karl Friston
videos.s: Neuroscientist Karl Friston gives a short talk on the free energy principle, covering Markov blankets, Bayesian model evidence and global brain theories.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a high-level introduction to the brain as a predictive, statistical machine.

videos.t: Jeff Hawkins: Thousand Brains Theory of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #25
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews Jeff Hawkins of Numenta about the Thousand Brains Theory and how the neocortex might be reverse-engineered. They also cover hierarchical temporal memory and brain-inspired AI.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it to hear Hawkins explain his theory himself, including reference frames and the old versus new brain.

videos.t: The Default Mode Network & End of Suffering - Gary Weber
videos.s: A dialogue with Gary Weber on the default mode network, meditation and non-dual awakening, touching on psychedelics, thought and time. It is part of the Non-Dual Couch series.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as an example of how meditation may switch off the default mode network.

videos.t: Edward Gibson: Human Language, Psycholinguistics, Syntax, Grammar & LLMs | Lex Fridman Podcast #426
videos.s: Lex Fridman interviews MIT psycholinguist Edward Gibson on human language, syntax and grammar, and how large language models relate to them. The conversation runs nearly three hours.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for the claim that LLMs capture the form of language but not meaning, and for how the brain's language network works.

videos.t: Diatoms: Tiny Factories You Can See From Space
videos.s: An episode of Journey to the Microcosmos, hosted by Hank Green, about diatoms, single-celled algae with glass shells. It covers their role in producing a large share of Earth's oxygen and uses such as beer filtering.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for microscope footage and a clear introduction to diatoms and their share of Earth's oxygen.

videos.t: Irving Kirsch:  The Emperor's New Drugs
videos.s: Psychologist Irving Kirsch gives a distinguished lecture on antidepressant trials and the placebo effect. He argues drug-placebo differences are small outside severe depression.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as evidence against the serotonin model and for how much placebo drives antidepressant response.

videos.t: The Super-Fast Logistics of Delivering Blood By Drone
videos.s: A Wendover Productions video on how Zipline delivers blood and medical supplies by drone in Rwanda. It covers the catapult launch, parachute drop and the logistics behind the service.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a detailed look at blood delivery by drone from a channel that covers global logistics.

videos.t: You Are Immune Against Every Disease
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animation on the human immune system, describing the body as an ecosystem and how immune defenses cope with the variety of invaders. It also promotes their book Immune.
videos.w: Commenters say it shows how remarkable the immune system is, including how it handles variations of invaders.

videos.t: Shawn Douglas - Nanoscale Instruments for Visualizing Small Proteins & Bret Victor - Dynamicland
videos.s: A Foresight Institute workshop video with two talks: Shawn Douglas on nanoscale instruments for visualizing small proteins, and Bret Victor on Dynamicland. Victor's part shows biomolecular design built with physical objects in his Realtalk system.
videos.w: Commenters point to Victor's segment as a demo of how far Dynamicland can be pushed into a specialised domain such as biomolecular design.

videos.t: I have APHANTASIA (and you may too...without realising it!)
videos.s: An artist describes discovering she has aphantasia, the inability to form mental images, and how it affects her drawing work. She includes a test and asks viewers about their own visualization.
videos.w: Commenters say it describes the feeling of aphantasia well and includes a way to test yourself.

videos.t: Why Women Are Stripey
videos.s: Veritasium explains X-chromosome inactivation, where different cells in a woman's body switch off different X chromosomes, giving a mosaic pattern. It links this to calico cat coloring.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for the genetics behind mosaic patterns in women and in calico cats.

videos.t: AlphaFold - The Most Useful Thing AI Has Ever Done
videos.s: A Veritasium video on AlphaFold, DeepMind's protein structure prediction system, and the protein design work it enabled. It includes interviews with John Jumper and with David Baker's protein design group.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a clear explanation of AlphaFold and why protein folding prediction matters.

videos.t: Vaccines: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
videos.s: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on vaccines, arguing that the benefits far outweigh the minuscule risks and looking at why some parents still doubt their safety.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a good episode on why vaccines matter.

videos.t: What Is the RNA World Hypothesis?
videos.s: Stated Clearly explains the RNA world hypothesis, which resolves the chicken-or-egg problem of genes versus enzymes by proposing that RNA once did both jobs.
videos.w: Commenters call it an engaging overview of how evolution could begin with RNA chains alone.

videos.t: Wim Hof Method Guided Breathing for Beginners (3 Rounds Slow Pace)
videos.s: A guided Wim Hof breathing session of three rounds at a slow pace, building from a 30 second to a 90 second breath hold. An on-screen bubble animation helps keep the rhythm.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an easier guided session for beginners, and one person uses it as a sleep aid.

videos.t: Why hierarchy creates a destructive force within the human psyche (by dr. Robert Sapolsky)
videos.s: A short clip of Robert Sapolsky on how social hierarchy generates chronic stress, drawing on baboon research. He links rank-related stress to heart health and life expectancy.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a short explanation of how stress in hierarchical arrangements affects heart health and lifespan.

videos.t: Is Your Red The Same as My Red?
videos.s: Vsauce explores qualia and whether different people experience colors the same way, drawing on color blindness, Mary's room, the explanatory gap and subjective experience.
videos.w: Commenters call it a good video on qualia and subjective color.

videos.t: Vitamin D and Immunity, Lots of Evidence
videos.s: Dr. John Campbell reviews studies on vitamin D deficiency and immunity, including links to influenza and COVID-19, with Public Health England advice. He walks through the sources he cites.
videos.w: Commenters share it as an evidence-focused doctor overview, noting that vitamin D is cheap with minimal downside.

videos.t: Dr. Matthew Phillips - 'Metabolic Strategies as Therapies in Cancer and Neurodegeneration'
videos.s: Neurologist Dr. Matthew Phillips talks at Low Carb Gold Coast 2022 about fasting and ketogenic diets as therapies for cancer and neurodegenerative disease. He focuses on mitochondrial dysfunction and brain energy metabolism.
videos.w: Commenters say it is worth a listen for metabolic therapy in cancer and neurodegeneration, including fasting.

videos.t: All you need to know to understand 5G
videos.s: Physicist Sabine Hossenfelder explains how 5G works and examines the health concerns around millimeter wave radiation. She reviews the scientific evidence and the open letters from scientists.
videos.w: Commenters suggest it to 5G skeptics as an even-handed take noting that few long-term millimeter wave studies exist.

videos.t: Debunking Dr. Robert Lustig's Claims from The Huberman Lab Podcast | Educational Video | Biolayne
videos.s: Dr. Layne Norton critiques claims made by Dr. Robert Lustig on the Huberman Lab podcast, checking them against the nutrition research with cited sources. It covers topics such as sugar, calories and fruit juice.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as the rebuttal to Lustig claims from that Huberman episode.

videos.t: What is the best diet for humans? | Eran Segal | TEDxRuppin
videos.s: Prof. Eran Segal TEDx talk on research showing that blood sugar responses to identical foods vary widely between people. He describes an algorithm that predicts individual responses and why one best diet for everyone does not exist.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for the finding that food effects depend on the person, including their gut bacteria.

videos.t: Update on my Brain Injury & the Future of Strange Parts
videos.s: An update from the Strange Parts YouTuber on his recovery from a brain injury caused by a metal pipe while filming, and his plans for the channel.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a creator account of recovering from a severe concussion, including bad medical advice.

videos.t: David Sinclair | Why We Age and Why We Don't Have To | Talks at Google
videos.s: Harvard geneticist David Sinclair discusses his book Lifespan at Google. He covers the biology of aging, lifestyle interventions and possible future ways to slow or reverse it.
videos.w: Commenters share it as an hour-long talk by the book author on reversing aging and cell reprogramming.

videos.t: How the Krebs cycle powers life and death – with Nick Lane
videos.s: Biochemist Nick Lane gives a Royal Institution lecture arguing that the Krebs cycle is central to what makes cells alive, not just genetic information. He links metabolism to the origin of life, death and aging.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a good talk from an excellent science communicator on the chemistry of life and mitochondria.

videos.t: Gay Frogs: A Deep Dive
videos.s: A long video essay on the claim that chemicals such as atrazine are feminizing frogs. It covers the science, the EPA and the role of chemical companies.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a thorough review of the claim and an example of regulatory capture over toxic chemicals.

videos.t: Why Meat is the Best Worst Thing in the World 🍔
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt animated explainer on meat: why people love it and what it costs animals, the environment and health. It lays out the trade-offs of meat production and consumption.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an eloquent video that makes people stop and think about the cost of eating meat.

videos.t: Optimizing Workspace for Productivity, Focus, & Creativity
videos.s: A Huberman Lab episode on setting up a workspace for productivity, focus and creativity, covering light, posture, movement and sound. It touches on ceiling height and the effect of screens on the brain.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for ideas such as the cathedral effect and how white noise and screens affect brain function.

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1027 - Courtney Dauwalter
videos.s: Joe Rogan interviews ultramarathon runner Courtney Dauwalter shortly after she won the Moab 240 in under 58 hours. She tells stories of enduring extreme fatigue and hallucinations.
videos.w: Commenters point to her stories of persevering through physical fatigue and hallucinations.

videos.t: How Smoking vs Vaping Affects Your Lungs  ● You Must See This ! !
videos.s: A demonstration of what a month of vaping versus a month of smoking does to the lungs, using a filter to show the residue. It is part of a series of similar experiments.
videos.w: Commenters send it to people who claim vaping might be worse than smoking, as a graphic comparison of lung impact.

videos.t: How Children Develop Perfect Pitch
videos.s: Rick Beato discusses a theory of why some children develop perfect pitch, based on early exposure to music, drawing on his experience with his own children.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as an explanation of how early exposure to complex music can build perfect pitch.

videos.t: Mitochondria: the cell's powerhouse
videos.s: A short Harvard animation narrated by Professor Rob Lue introducing mitochondria as the powerhouses of the cell and how cells turn food and oxygen into energy.
videos.w: Commenters call it a beautiful animation that also explains why we breathe oxygen.

videos.t: Dr. Robert Sapolsky's lecture about Biological Underpinnings of Religiosity
videos.s: Robert Sapolsky Stanford lecture on the biological underpinnings of religiosity, from his human behavioral biology course. It covers theories linking religion to stress and to schizotypal traits.
videos.w: Commenters point to it for theories on how religion may reduce stress and depression and on schizotypal individuals in religious roles.

videos.t: Your Brain at Work
videos.s: David Rock gives a Google Tech Talk based on his book Your Brain at Work, using neuroscience to explain why focus and productivity are hard at the office. He gives strategies for managing mental energy and distraction.
videos.w: Commenters call it interesting for developers and knowledge workers, including the SCARF model of workplace threat and reward.

videos.t: Try this bizarre audio illusion! 👁️👂😮 - BBC
videos.s: A BBC Horizon clip demonstrating the McGurk effect, where the same audio sounds like different syllables depending on the mouth movements you see.
videos.w: Commenters call it the most compelling illustration of the brain fooling itself and of vision altering what we hear.

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #1385 - Paul Stamets
videos.s: A long Joe Rogan Experience interview with mycologist Paul Stamets about fungi, medicinal mushrooms and bioremediation.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a long interview that inspired them to read more about fungi.

videos.t: The Physics of Life (ft. It's Okay to be Smart & PBS Eons!)
videos.s: PBS Space Time, with It is Okay to be Smart and PBS Eons, asks how a universe drifting toward disorder produced something as complex as life. It presents the idea that thermodynamics may favor the emergence of life.
videos.w: Commenters call it a very good basic explanation of life and entropy, with references.

videos.t: The Man With The Seven Second Memory
videos.s: A documentary on Clive Wearing, a renowned musician whose brain was damaged by a virus in 1985, leaving him with a memory spanning only about seven seconds. It follows his life and condition.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as an extended documentary on an extreme case of amnesia.

videos.t: The man who faked human cloning
videos.s: BobbyBroccoli first of two long documentaries about Hwang Woo-suk, the South Korean scientist who faked human cloning results. It tells the story of the scandal that shook a country.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a documentary on scientific fraud and the history of human cloning research.

videos.t: Joe Rogan Experience #965 -  Robert Sapolsky
videos.s: Joe Rogan interviews Stanford neuroendocrinologist Robert Sapolsky about his book Behave. They discuss the biology of human behavior, including toxoplasmosis and risk-taking, and baboon troop dynamics.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as an interview with a superstar of the field, with long discussion of toxoplasma and risk-taking.

videos.t: The Battle of the Diets: Is Anyone Winning (At Losing?)
videos.s: Stanford researcher Christopher Gardner presents his large comparison of four popular diets under real-world conditions, in which the lowest-carbohydrate Atkins diet came out on top.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a researcher presenting study results, including benefits of low-carb diets, alongside several other studies.

videos.t: This Is Your Brain On Stale Air
videos.s: Tom Scott features Kurtis Baute inside a sealed homemade biodome as carbon dioxide builds up, showing how stale air with elevated CO2 affects cognitive function. Sources include studies on CO2 and cognitive scores.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it as a good starting point for CO2 effects, noting the body senses elevated CO2 poorly.

videos.t: Is Our Food Becoming Less Nutritious?
videos.s: Veritasium examines whether food has become less nutritious, weighing soil depletion, selective breeding and rising atmospheric CO2. It shows nutrient decline even in weeds over a century.
videos.w: Commenters call it a short explainer that puts declining crop nutrition in context, including the role of CO2.

videos.t: Why Don't You Want To Do Anything After Binging 4 Hours of YouTube Videos...
videos.s: Dr. K of HealthyGamerGG explains why people feel unmotivated and unable to start tasks after hours of YouTube or similar distractions. He frames it as a result of how social media is designed to capture attention.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a more scientific explanation of why screen binges dull motivation, relevant to internet addiction.

videos.t: Milton Friedman Speaks: The Economics of Medical Care (B1234) - Full Video
videos.s: Milton Friedman lectures to physicians on the economics of medical care, arguing that government involvement raises costs and leads toward socialized medicine. He also discusses licensing and protecting patients from quacks.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for his argument that regulation and lobbying lead to a centrally planned healthcare system.

videos.t: Apple Watch : Scientific Sleep Test
videos.s: The Quantified Scientist, a sleep researcher, tests Apple Watch sleep tracking against a research-grade Dreem 2 headband, comparing accuracy for sleep stages, deep and REM sleep.
videos.w: Commenters value it as a data-focused review of tracker accuracy by a professional sleep scientist.

videos.t: altitude chamber hypoxia training guy passes out
videos.s: Footage of FAA altitude chamber hypoxia training for pilots in which a participant passes out from oxygen deprivation. It shows how quickly and subtly cognition fails at altitude.
videos.w: Commenters point to it to see how fast oxygen deprivation takes effect.

videos.t: The next outbreak? We’re not ready | Bill Gates | TED
videos.s: Bill Gates 2015 TED talk, given after the 2014 Ebola outbreak, argues the world is unprepared for the next fast-spreading epidemic. He calls for scenario planning, vaccine research and trained health workers.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as an advance warning of pandemic unpreparedness whose details resemble the coronavirus outbreak.

videos.t: Your Coffee Addiction Is Probably Good for You
videos.s: CGP Grey short explainer arguing that caffeine addiction is mostly harmless and may even be beneficial. It covers what caffeine does in the body.
videos.w: Commenters call it a nice explanation of caffeine effects, with its benefits and few negatives.

videos.t: Is Organic Really Better? Healthy Food or Trendy Scam?
videos.s: A Kurzgesagt explainer asking whether organic food is really healthier or better for the environment. It defines what organic means and looks at pesticide use, nutrition and environmental impact, with sources.
videos.w: Commenters recommend it for clarifying what organic means and for its sourced look at pesticides and nutrition.

videos.t: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325
videos.s: Lex Fridman talks with Tufts biologist Michael Levin about bioelectricity, embryogenesis, xenobots and how cells collectively pursue goals. They range into cognition, evolution and the possibility of aliens.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as a long-form introduction to Levin on cells as goal-directed, including cancer as cells losing their purpose.

videos.t: 7 Years (A Life In Medicine)
videos.s: A song by Zubin Damania (ZDoggMD) about a life in medicine, from training through practice.
videos.w: A commenter calls it an uplifting pick-me-up for people in medicine.

videos.t: Coronavirus in Italy - Report From The Front Lines
videos.s: A JAMA Network interview with an Italian intensive care chief on the COVID-19 surge in Italy's hospitals.
videos.w: A commenter calls it an excellent interview worth sharing with colleagues.

videos.t: Matthew Broussard Stand-Up 07/25/16 | CONAN on TBS
videos.s: A stand-up set by Matthew Broussard on Conan with medical content.
videos.w: A commenter praises it as medically accurate stand-up comedy.

videos.t: Making House Calls, To People Without Homes
videos.s: A NationSwell profile of a doctor who makes house calls to people experiencing homelessness.
videos.w: Commenters share it as a reminder of why people go into medicine, noting he helps over 1,200 homeless people a year.

videos.t: The American Health Care Act: A Republican Response to The Affordable Care Act
videos.s: A Healthcare Triage breakdown of the Republican American Health Care Act proposed to replace the Affordable Care Act.
videos.w: Commenters call it a more level-headed and objective explanation of the bill than other videos, though left-leaning.

videos.t: If Homeopathy Beats Science
videos.s: A satirical comedy sketch lampooning homeopathy.
videos.w: A commenter says the sketch nails the absurdity of homeopathy.

videos.t: Evelyn Yang reveals she was sexually assaulted while pregnant
videos.s: A CNN segment in which Evelyn Yang says she was sexually assaulted by her obstetrician while pregnant.
videos.w: A commenter calls the personal testimony incredibly moving and worth watching.

videos.t: First Day of Rural Medicine
videos.s: A video from Dr. Glaucomflecken about a first day in rural medicine.
videos.w: A student says it captures why they want to practice rural medicine.

videos.t: Embryology of the Pharyngeal Arches (Easy to Understand)
videos.s: An easy-to-follow lecture on the embryology of the pharyngeal arches.
videos.w: A commenter says it made pharyngeal arches finally clear.

videos.t: Investment Banker vs. Lawyer vs. Doctor Salaries - Who Gets Paid The Most?
videos.s: A rareliquid video comparing the pay and training length of investment bankers, lawyers and doctors.
videos.w: A commenter says the creator did a good job researching how long it takes to become a doctor.

videos.t: Sketchy Medical - Coronavirus (Coronaviridae) [UPDATED]
videos.s: Updated Sketchy Medical video on the coronavirus family.
videos.w: Recommended to students who have not yet seen the updated Sketchy coronavirus video.

videos.t: Paralyzed man walks after bluetooth connects his brain and spine
videos.s: An Associated Press news report on a paralyzed man who walks again using a wireless brain-spine interface.
videos.w: A commenter shares it as a cool story about a brain-spine interface restoring walking.

videos.t: You wanna hurt me?
videos.s: A short comforting clip that a medical student watches after getting harsh clinical evaluations.
videos.w: A commenter uses it as a pick-me-up whenever evaluations come back harsh.

videos.t: Protect Patient Safety: Stop HB 4359
videos.s: An advocacy video by MI SafeCare arguing against a Michigan bill that would give CRNAs independence from anesthesiologists.
videos.w: A commenter says physicians should make more videos like this to explain the difference between midlevels and doctors.

videos.t: Nursing research leaders: NPs should not work alone in the ER
videos.s: A Patients at Risk video on nursing research leaders saying nurse practitioners should not work alone in the emergency room.
videos.w: Physicians use it as pushback against nurse practitioner and PA scope expansion.

videos.t: CaRMS Match for Couples
videos.s: A short explainer on how couples matching works in the Canadian CaRMS residency match.
videos.w: A commenter points to it to explain how couples can match together.

videos.t: Understanding Jugular Venous Pressure JVP
videos.s: An explainer on jugular venous pressure and how to understand and read it.
videos.w: A commenter says it made JVP stick for good.

videos.t: Shoulder Roll Progressions for Increasing Scapular Mobility with Antranik
videos.s: Antranik Kizirian demonstrates shoulder roll progressions to increase scapular mobility, with form notes on posture and flexibility.
videos.w: A commenter found it super helpful for questions about scapular depression, posture and mobility.

videos.t: Golden Nuggets Podcast Episode #1 w/ strategypattern and Jamesb
videos.s: First episode of the Golden Nuggets Podcast on flashcard formulation, card quality and keeping decks.
videos.w: Commenters say it is useful for newcomers and highlights how many shared decks favor quantity over quality.

videos.t: DON'T TRUST THE HEADLINES: A critical review of 'Value of NP Inpatient Hospital Staffing"
videos.s: A Patients at Risk video critiquing a study on nurse practitioner inpatient hospital staffing.
videos.w: Physicians use it as pushback against nurse practitioner and PA scope expansion.

videos.t: When Your “Doctor” Isn’t a Doctor | What They Don’t Tell You
videos.s: Kevin Jubbal, M.D. discusses midlevel providers presenting themselves as doctors, with real examples.
videos.w: Commenters note he uses his platform to argue forcefully against midlevel encroachment.

videos.t: Perineal Pouches Part 1
videos.s: Part 1 of an Access Anatomy lesson on the perineal pouches and the regions of the pelvis.
videos.w: Students say it explains the perineal regions and pouches clearly.

videos.t: In Clinic (In Paris medical school parody)
videos.s: A high-production music video parodying In Paris, with lyrics about medical school clinic life.
videos.w: Commenters praise the production value and say the lyrics were fun and helped them prep for Step.

videos.t: Tutorial of Image Occlusion 2.0 for Anki 2.0
videos.s: A tutorial on the Anki Image Occlusion 2.0 add-on, including how to group items on an image.
videos.w: Commenters say it is a huge help for anatomy and explains grouping items well.

videos.t: A Boy Ate 25 Laxative Brownies In 1 Hour. This Is What Happened To His Kidneys.
videos.s: A Chubbyemu video on a case of a boy who ate 25 laxative brownies in an hour and what happened to his kidneys, told as a narrated medical case.
videos.w: Commenters describe the channel as an intriguing series on medical anomalies, though not super medical.

videos.t: FCVS TRICK | Check if You Are Pass or Fail Ahead of Results #usmle #usmlestep1 #ecfmg
videos.s: A walkthrough of signing up to see USMLE pass or fail results early through FCVS.
videos.w: Commenters followed it to sign up for early results.

videos.t: We Need to Rethink Exercise (Updated Version)
videos.s: Kurzgesagt explains why exercise alone does little for weight loss, since the body compensates by adjusting its total energy expenditure. It argues exercise is still very valuable for health.
videos.w: Commenters cite it as a decent pop-science summary of how the body offsets the calories burned in exercise.

videos.t: I Grew Real Spider Silk Using Yeast
videos.s: The Thought Emporium shows how they engineered a yeast strain to produce real spider silk, after more than two years of lab work and many failures. The video explains the genetic engineering process behind it.
videos.w: Commenters point to it as an example of cutting-edge biotech becoming as accessible as computing in the 1980s.

videos.t: ATP synthase in action
videos.s: A short Harvard Online animation, narrated by Professor Rob Lue, showing how ATP synthase works inside mitochondria. It comes from the HarvardX Cell Biology: Mitochondria course.
videos.w: Commenters like the visualization of ATP synthase rotating to make ATP, likening it to a tiny turbine.

videos.t: You Need to Be Bored. Here's Why.
videos.s: Harvard professor Arthur Brooks explains why boredom is useful rather than something to avoid. He describes how a wandering mind engages the default mode network, which supports creativity and curiosity, and suggests it may protect against depression.
videos.w: Commenters cite it for the case that boredom sparks curiosity and is harder than ever to find.
